bells.name: Sext
bells.text: Noon. The sun, such as it is.

bells.name: Compline
bells.text: Night. Somewhere to sleep, or not.

age.title: Age
age.description: How many years the character has.

levels.2: Grown.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: How you look to a stranger: what you're wearing, and how it wears you.

levels.2: Plain.
Knows how to stand, and where to hit.
levels.5: Fights like someone who has done it often.
levels.6: Other fighters notice how you stand.

levels.1: Put them to rest: someone you lost works bound. Find them, and buy their release.
levels.2: Rise: be the one who stamps the seals, not the one who wears them.
levels.3: Get even: someone took your place. Make them pay.

aspiration-stage.title: Aspiration stage
aspiration-stage.description: How far the character's aspiration has come.

levels.2: Feminine.

binder.title: Binder
binder.description: You can bind the dead. You have no licence, and binding without one is a crime.

levels.1: A hedge-binder. Your hands are always cold.

levels.2: Strong enough for an honest day's work.
levels.3: Calloused, and starting to look it.
levels.5: Carries what two others would.
levels.6: People ask you to move the heavy things.

chill.title: The Binder's Chill
chill.description: What binding takes from the binder: warmth first, then years, then memory. No coat and no fire helps.

levels.2: Cold to the elbow. You sleep in your gloves.
levels.3: Grey at the temples. A name you knew is gone.
levels.5: Old before your time. Whole summers missing.
levels.7: Hollow. Something is left, and it is cold.

chill.changeUp: The cold goes deeper, and stays.

chill-binder.title: The chapel binder's Binder's Chill
chill-binder.description: What binding has cost [who:regard-binder] since you met her. When she releases a pauper for nothing, she pays the whole cost herself.

levels.1: Colder than when you met her.

chill-binder.changeUp: Binding takes a little more from [who:regard-binder].

claim.title: Claim
claim.description: Who holds your death. Nobody gets inside the walls without a claim.

levels.1: The church holds your death. A term of labour, then release.
levels.2: The company holds your death. They will work you until you fall apart.
levels.3: The burial club holds your death. Its binder will release you at once.

claim-held.title: A claim
claim-held.description: Anyone's claim on your death: a seal at your neck, and most likely a mark on your skin.

clerks-clothes.title: A clerk's black
clerks-clothes.description: Good cloth, brushed thin. It says you can read.

club-dues-days.title: Days to the club's dues
club-dues-days.description: Hidden: the days until the burial club's dues come again.

club-dues-owed.title: Days the club's dues are owed
club-dues-owed.plural: Days the club's dues are owed
club-dues-owed.description: Hidden: 1 on the day the dues come, 2 when they are a day late.

coat.title: A coat
coat.description: Rolled up and tied to your belt. Warm, if you put it on.

cold.title: Cold
cold.description: The weather, getting into you. It rises while what you wear is not warm enough for the weather, and falls when it is. Each piece of clothing shows its Warmth in the Kit. Makes Shot and Guile tests harder: numb fingers. Lying still in it, cold enough to notice is too cold to sleep.

levels.5: Shivering.

cold.changeUp: The weather gets through what you're wearing. The cold bites deeper.

crisis.title: The crisis
crisis.description: What is happening to the city right now.

levels.2: The grain fleet is lost.
levels.5: Everything is tightening.

crisis-bread-days.title: Days until the baker's new price
crisis-bread-days.plural: Days until the baker's new price
crisis-bread-days.description: Hidden: the days before the crisis card about bread joins the camp's deck.

crisis-bread-dear.title: Bread
crisis-bread-dear.description: What bread costs below the wall, while the fleet is late.

levels.1: Dearer than it was. The baker blames the fleet.

crisis-claim-talk.title: Bread by the claim
crisis-claim-talk.description: What the camp says the council will do, now that the fleet is lost.

levels.1: Talk at every fire: the council will give bread only to people with a claim.

crisis-dead-days.title: Days until the camp's dead mount
crisis-dead-days.plural: Days until the camp's dead mount
crisis-dead-days.description: Hidden: the days before the crisis card about the camp's dead joins the camp's deck.

crisis-dead-unheld.title: The camp's dead
crisis-dead-unheld.description: The dead of the camp below the wall, and who comes for them.

levels.1: More every morning, and fewer with anyone to come for them. The burial club asks more dues.

crisis-gate-days.title: Days until the gate tightens
crisis-gate-days.description: Hidden: the days before the crisis card about the gate joins the camp's deck.

crisis-gate-tight.title: The gate
crisis-gate-tight.description: How the wardens treat arrivals, while the fleet is late.

levels.1: The wardens turn back more every morning. The chapel asks more for a claim.

crisis-made-room.title: Made room by the fire for a family turned back
crisis-made-room.plural: Made room by the fire for a family turned back

crisis-moved-them-on.title: Moved a family turned back away from the fire
crisis-moved-them-on.plural: Moved a family turned back away from the fire

crisis-news-days.title: Days until the news
crisis-news-days.description: Hidden: the days before the news from the ford joins the camp's deck.

crisis-paid-for-a-loaf.title: Paid the coin a woman was short for bread
crisis-paid-for-a-loaf.plural: Paid the coin a woman was short for bread

crisis-read-the-list.title: Read the list of the camp's dead aloud
crisis-read-the-list.plural: Read the list of the camp's dead aloud

crisis-took-a-loaf.title: Took a loaf from the baker's cart
crisis-took-a-loaf.plural: Took a loaf from the baker's cart

crisis-walked-past-the-list.title: Walked past the list of the camp's dead
crisis-walked-past-the-list.plural: Walked past the list of the camp's dead

debt.title: Debt
debt.description: What you owe, and to whom.

levels.5: A debt that could ruin you.

depth-camp.title: Further out
depth-camp.description: How far out into the camp you are today, from the gate and the haulers' fire. The further out, the poorer the fires, and the less the people there have to lose.

levels.0: Back among the fires you know.
levels.2: Among strangers, below the yards.
levels.3: The far camp, where people have nothing to lose.
levels.4: The last fires, as far out as the camp goes.

desire.title: Desire
desire.description: The body's other hunger. It grows by the day.

levels.5: Aching.

desire.changeUp: A restless want stirs in you.

drowned-mans-boots.title: A drowned man's boots
drowned-mans-boots.description: Good leather, a little shrunk. The river had them first.

eye.title: Eye
eye.description: A temperament. You watch, and learn, and wait.
eye.changeUp: You stood back and watched how it went. Eye grows to [qb:eye]. [Temperaments rise at moments like this one. Each opens choices that only that kind of person would see.]

familiarity-camp.title: Familiarity
familiarity-camp.description: How well you know the camp below the wall: its fires, its people and its ways round. You learn it by walking it, by talking, and by working.

levels.2: Known by sight.
levels.4: At home here, as much as anyone is.

feathered-hat.title: A broad hat with a feather
feathered-hat.plural: A broad hat with a feather
feathered-hat.description: Black felt, a brim wide enough for shade, and one long feather, dyed.

feature-broad-and-heavy.title: Broad and heavy
feature-broad-and-heavy.description: Built for work. Hunger comes faster.

feature-limp.title: A limp
feature-limp.description: Slower on the road and in flight.

feature-maimed-hand.title: Maimed hand
feature-maimed-hand.description: A rope or a blade took fingers. Fine work is harder.

feature-pox-scarred.title: Pox-scarred
feature-pox-scarred.description: Survived the pox. Some think you immune; some think you carry it.

feature-slight.title: Slight
feature-slight.description: Overlooked, underestimated, and fits through tight places.

feature-striking.title: Striking
feature-striking.description: Doors open, and so does unwanted attention.

feature-tall.title: Tall
feature-tall.description: Seen over any crowd, and hard to hide.

features-picked.title: Features picked
features-picked.description: Hidden: how many features the character has picked in customisation (0, 1 or 2).

fieldcraft.title: Fieldcraft
fieldcraft.description: Surviving outside the walls: foraging, tracking, weather, the river.

levels.2: Can find water, and the way back.
levels.3: Finds food and shelter when you must.
levels.4: Reads the weather and the ground.
levels.5: Reads the weather, the ground, and who crossed it.
levels.6: Finds the way in the dark, and food in the mud.
levels.7: Nothing crosses the river or the road without you knowing.

fingerless-gloves.title: Fingerless gloves
fingerless-gloves.description: Knitted, the thumbs worn through. Good for rope, and for counting coin in the cold.

flair.title: Flair
flair.description: Flair shows how well your clothes match the style you chose. Each worn item that adds points to your chosen style raises Flair.

levels.3: Your clothes show a hint of a style.
levels.5: Your clothes look put together.

foreign-sash.title: A dyed sash
foreign-sash.description: A length of silk that goes twice round the waist. Its colour has no name here.

full-game.title: Full game
full-game.description: Hidden: never set in the demo. A choice that requires it is locked.

levels.2: Keeps a straight face, and your own counsel.
levels.5: People believe you, the first time.
levels.6: Walks in and out, and nobody remembers.
levels.7: Nobody ever sees you coming or going.

hardship.title: Hardship
hardship.description: What a rough life takes out of you, body and mind. A night on the ground adds to it; a night in a bed eases it. Makes Nerve and Presence tests harder.

levels.5: Fraying.
levels.7: At the end of your rope.

hardship.changeUp: It takes something out of you.

haulers-clothes.title: Hauler's clothes
haulers-clothes.description: Canvas and leather, worn through at the shoulder where the rope sat.

hopeful.title: Hopeful
hopeful.description: A printed share in your pocket, and a picture in your head.

hunger.title: Hunger
hunger.description: An empty belly, and getting emptier. Makes Brawn and Nerve tests harder.

levels.5: Ravenous.

keepsake-anatomist-page.title: A page from the anatomist's book
keepsake-anatomist-page.plural: A page from the anatomist's book
keepsake-anatomist-page.description: A cheap printed copy. A drawing of a dead man's head, opened, with letters on every part.

keepsake-ashes.title: A pouch of ashes
keepsake-ashes.description: Your own dead, burned your own way. Nobody works them.

keepsake-company-seal.title: A pewter seal
keepsake-company-seal.description: A company claim, stamped with a mark that is not yours. The company still holds the one who wore it.

keepsake-handbell.title: A drover's handbell
keepsake-handbell.description: Cracked. Your uncle carried it for twenty years. It rings flat now.

keepsake-knife.title: A parent's knife
keepsake-knife.description: Notched once for each risen it put down, back when families put down their own.

keepsake-lock-of-hair.title: A lock of hair
keepsake-lock-of-hair.description: Cut before a company took the body.

keepsake-nail.title: A pulled nail
keepsake-nail.description: Bought out of a company's labour with everything your family had. Someone you loved lies still because of it.

keepsake-shore-share.title: A share in a ship
keepsake-shore-share.description: A printed share in a ship across the sea. Whoever bought it never sailed.

knife.title: First Strike
knife.description: A temperament. You do the hard thing first, and fast.
knife.changeUp: You did the hard thing, fast, before anyone could stop you. First Strike grows to [qb:knife]. [Temperaments rise at moments like this one. Each opens choices that only that kind of person would see.]

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: Reading, writing, the registers, forging, contracts.

levels.2: Reads and writes a plain hand.
levels.3: Reads fast, and writes a clean hand.
levels.4: Reads a contract, and finds the catch in it.
levels.5: Reads fast, and spots what has been crossed out.
levels.6: Writes a hand that clerks respect.
levels.7: Could forge a register and not be caught.

mark-fresh.title: A fresh mark
mark-fresh.description: Your claim's mark, still healing. It takes three nights. Until it heals, the wardens can't read it, and the gate won't take you.

levels.1: One more night. In the morning the wardens can read your mark.
levels.2: Two more nights before the wardens can read your mark.
levels.3: Three nights before your mark heals. Until then the wardens can't read it.

merchants-doublet.title: A merchant's doublet
merchants-doublet.description: Slashed sleeves lined with red silk. A merchant was buried in less.

met-binder.title: Met the chapel binder
met-binder.description: Hidden: the character has been introduced to the chapel binder.

met-rope-mother.title: Met the rope-mother
met-rope-mother.description: Hidden: the character has been introduced to the rope-mother.

met-surgeon.title: Met the surgeon
met-surgeon.description: Hidden: the surgeon by the road told you his name.

met-yard-keeper.title: Met the yard-keeper
met-yard-keeper.description: Hidden: the character has been introduced to the yard-keeper.

met-young-man.title: Met the young man from the farms
met-young-man.plural: Met the young man from the farms
met-young-man.description: Hidden: the young man at the fire told you his name.

mourning-ring.title: A silver mourning ring
mourning-ring.description: A small silver skull sits on top of the ring. Inside the band, someone has engraved the words "Remember me".

nerve.title: Nerve
nerve.description: Facing the dead, pain, threats, the proofs.

levels.2: Still rattled, but you hide it.
levels.3: Your hands shake after, not during.
levels.5: Keeps a level head when others scream.
levels.6: Looks at the dead and doesn't blink.

novices-clothes.title: A novice's grey
novices-clothes.description: The church's grey, with the badge picked off.

numb.title: Numb
numb.description: Past feeling much of anything, for now.

levels.1: Numb to it all, for now.

oilcloth-cape.title: A drover's oilcloth cape
oilcloth-cape.description: Black, stiff with wax, and long enough to sit on. The rain runs off it like off a roof.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: Where the character comes from, and what they left.

levels.1: The farmlands. The dead plough your family's fields now.
levels.2: The river. The company's dead took your rope.
levels.4: A broken town. You walked out of the dead lands.
levels.5: Another city. Smaller, and behind you.
levels.6: The church. You left before your vows.

physick.title: Physick
physick.description: Wounds, fever, plague, examining the dead.

levels.1: Winces at the sight of a wound.
levels.2: Can look at a wound without turning away.
levels.3: Dresses a cut, and knows what to watch for.
levels.4: Sets a break, cleans a cut.
levels.5: Knows a fever before the patient does.
levels.6: Can tell what killed someone from how they lie.
levels.7: Reads a body the way a clerk reads a ledger.

pilgrims-badge.title: A lead pilgrim's badge
pilgrims-badge.description: A saint nobody here can name, stamped in lead, with a pin to wear it.

levels.2: Noticed, if you speak up.
levels.5: People listen, and remember what you said.
levels.6: People step aside before you ask.
levels.7: A voice that carries a room.

presence-binder.title: Where the chapel binder is
presence-binder.description: Hidden: whether the binder is in the chapel and able to talk.

levels.2: Busy.

presence-rope-mother.title: Where the rope-mother is
presence-rope-mother.description: Hidden: whether the rope-mother is at the fire and able to talk.

levels.2: Busy.

presence-young-man.title: Where the young man is
presence-young-man.description: Hidden: whether the young man is at the haulers' fire and able to talk. 0 once he is dead.

prologue.title: The prologue
prologue.description: How far the character's story has come.

levels.1: On the road, with the city in sight.
levels.2: Turned back at the gate for want of a claim. The camp below the wall, waiting with everyone else for the grain fleet.
levels.3: Word came up the road from the ford: the grain fleet is lost.
levels.4: [who:young-man] died in the night, with no claim.
levels.5: Still outside the walls. The gate takes arrivals in the morning, and only with a claim's mark the wardens can read.
levels.7: The prologue ends. You know what you came for.

prologue-asked-about-the-shore.title: Asked when the ship sails
prologue-asked-about-the-shore.description: Hidden: the share-seller said it sails when it is full.

prologue-bed.title: A door behind the chapel
prologue-bed.description: Sister Ilse's room behind the chapel at the gate: a roof, a stove, and a door that shuts.

levels.1: [who:regard-binder] has offered you the floor of her room behind the chapel.
levels.2: You sleep at [who:regard-binder]'s, on a straw mattress by her stove, behind the chapel.

next.1: Go to the chapel at the gate at night, or when you're tired, and sleep at hers.

prologue-bed-last-night.title: Slept in Sister Ilse's home last night
prologue-bed-last-night.plural: Slept in Sister Ilse's home last night

prologue-bed-tonight.title: Slept in Sister Ilse's home tonight
prologue-bed-tonight.plural: Slept in Sister Ilse's home tonight

prologue-binder-flirted.title: Sister Ilse flirted back
prologue-binder-flirted.description: Hidden: you flirted with Sister Ilse, and she answered in kind.

prologue-binder-released-the-young-man.title: The chapel binder released the young man
prologue-binder-released-the-young-man.plural: The chapel binder released the young man
prologue-binder-released-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you carried him to the chapel, and the binder released him at once, for nothing, at her own cost.

prologue-binder-told-age.title: The binder told you her age
prologue-binder-told-age.plural: The binder told you her age

prologue-binder-told-claim.title: The binder told you what a church claim means
prologue-binder-told-claim.plural: The binder told you what a church claim means

prologue-binder-told-grey.title: You told the binder the grey suits her
prologue-binder-told-grey.plural: You told the binder the grey suits her

prologue-binder-told-paupers.title: The binder told you about the paupers
prologue-binder-told-paupers.plural: The binder told you about the paupers

prologue-binder-told-young-man.title: The binder talked about the young man
prologue-binder-told-young-man.plural: The binder talked about the young man

prologue-bought-a-share.title: Bought a share in a ship
prologue-bought-a-share.plural: Bought a share in a ship
prologue-bought-a-share.description: Hidden: you own a printed share in a ship across the sea.

prologue-bound-the-young-man.title: Bound the young man yourself
prologue-bound-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you bound him. You hold his binding, and he waits for you.

prologue-burned-the-young-man.title: Burned the young man
prologue-burned-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you helped the haulers burn him before the wardens came.

prologue-company-shifts.title: Shifts in the dead-yard
prologue-company-shifts.description: The shifts you have worked well in the company's dead-yard. The company signs only people who have shown they can do the work.

levels.1: One good shift in the dead-yard.
levels.2: Two good shifts in the dead-yard.
levels.3: Three good shifts in the dead-yard.
levels.4: Four good shifts. The company will sign you.

prologue-drain.title: A way under the wall
prologue-drain.description: Somewhere along the foot of the wall, there's a way into the city that doesn't go through the gate.

levels.1: There's a way under the wall somewhere. You keep an eye out for it.
levels.2: You're looking for it in earnest now: along the foot of the wall, downstream, where the tanneries are.
levels.3: Found: an old drain below the tanneries, big enough to crawl into.

next.1: Keep your eyes open as you get to know the camp.
next.2: Look along the wall when you explore the camp. You'll have to know the camp well to find it.

prologue-foraged-the-river.title: Foraged along the river
prologue-foraged-the-river.description: Hidden: you have foraged along the river once.

prologue-found-a-turnip.title: Found a turnip in the rut
prologue-found-a-turnip.plural: Found a turnip in the rut

prologue-found-the-company-tent.title: The crier showed you the company tent
prologue-found-the-company-tent.plural: The crier showed you the company tent
prologue-found-the-company-tent.description: Hidden: the company's crier pointed out the company tent and its shifts.

prologue-gave-the-bone-cart-a-hand.title: Gave the bone-cart a hand
prologue-gave-the-bone-cart-a-hand.description: Hidden: you have worked for the bone-cart once.

prologue-granted-a-weeks-grace.title: Granted a member of the club a week's grace
prologue-granted-a-weeks-grace.plural: Granted a member of the club a week's grace
prologue-granted-a-weeks-grace.description: Hidden: the box came back lighter, and the rope-mother remembers.

prologue-helped-with-the-dead.title: Helped with the camp's dead
prologue-helped-with-the-dead.description: Hidden: you have helped Sister Ilse with the camp's dead once.

prologue-hid-the-mark.title: Hid the mark
prologue-hid-the-mark.description: Hidden: you covered your claim's mark while it healed.

prologue-hired-out-the-young-man.title: Hired the young man out to the company
prologue-hired-out-the-young-man.plural: Hired the young man out to the company
prologue-hired-out-the-young-man.description: Hidden: he works in the company's dead-yard, and the company pays you for him.

prologue-holds-a-strangers-death.title: Holds a stranger's death
prologue-holds-a-strangers-death.description: Hidden: a man in the far camp sold you his claim. He wears your sign on a disc of lead, and you are to come for him before he rises.

prologue-laughed-at-the-shore.title: Laughed at the share-seller
prologue-laughed-at-the-shore.description: Hidden: you laughed at the share-seller, and a few people laughed with you.

prologue-lead-binder-killed.title: Lead: the fleet's binder was killed
prologue-lead-binder-killed.plural: Lead: the fleet's binder was killed
prologue-lead-binder-killed.description: At the ford, the fleet's binder was killed, and every hauling corpse broke loose in the water around the barges.

levels.1: The rider who came up the road to the camp, before the wardens took him. He said an arrow.

prologue-lead-dead-wear-seals.title: Lead: the dead wear their seals
prologue-lead-dead-wear-seals.plural: Lead: the dead wear their seals
prologue-lead-dead-wear-seals.description: The bound wear the seals they wore alive, nailed to the brow. You can read who owns each one.

levels.1: You were close enough to read them yourself.

prologue-lead-fleet-lost.title: Lead: the grain fleet is lost
prologue-lead-fleet-lost.plural: Lead: the grain fleet is lost
prologue-lead-fleet-lost.description: The grain fleet will not come. Something happened at the ford.

levels.1: The crowd in the camp below the wall. Nobody there saw it.

prologue-lead-the-drain.title: Lead: the old drain
prologue-lead-the-drain.description: An old drain runs under the wall below the tanneries. If it comes up anywhere, it comes up inside the walls.

prologue-lead-the-quays.title: Lead: the empty docks
prologue-lead-the-quays.description: The grain berths at the docks are empty, and the merchants are buying what grain there is.

levels.1: You went down and saw it yourself.

prologue-lead-the-seals.title: Lead: the wardens and the marks
prologue-lead-the-seals.plural: Lead: the wardens and the marks
prologue-lead-the-seals.description: Company brands go through first. Church marks get read. The rich show a seal and are bowed through. A fresh mark waits until it heals. One warden waves the burial club's knots through without a look.

levels.2: The people sleeping against the wall told you. They've had days to watch.

prologue-lead-the-theatre.title: Lead: the anatomy theatre
prologue-lead-the-theatre.description: The theatre where binding began is half shrine and half lecture hall. Pilgrims queue beside students.

levels.1: You went up and saw it yourself.

prologue-left-her-to-the-round.title: Left the rope-mother to carry the box alone
prologue-left-her-to-the-round.plural: Left the rope-mother to carry the box alone

prologue-left-the-young-man.title: Left the young man to the wardens
prologue-left-the-young-man.plural: Left the young man to the wardens
prologue-left-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you left him, and the wardens took his head on the road.

prologue-made-peace-with-the-mark.title: Made peace with the mark
prologue-made-peace-with-the-mark.description: Hidden: you looked at your claim's mark and took in what it means.

prologue-refused-a-weeks-grace.title: Refused a member of the club a week's grace
prologue-refused-a-weeks-grace.plural: Refused a member of the club a week's grace
prologue-refused-a-weeks-grace.description: Hidden: her place in the club lapsed, and her fire remembers your face.

prologue-release-today.title: Saw the old hauler released today
prologue-release-today.plural: Saw the old hauler released today

prologue-released-the-young-man.title: Unbound the young man
prologue-released-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you held his binding, and you drew the nail.

prologue-robbed-the-saver.title: Cut a seam of coin from the sleeping man's coat
prologue-robbed-the-saver.plural: Cut a seam of coin from the sleeping man's coat
prologue-robbed-the-saver.description: Hidden: 1, you got away with it; 2, he woke.

prologue-rope-mother-told-club.title: The rope-mother told you about the burial club
prologue-rope-mother-told-club.plural: The rope-mother told you about the burial club

prologue-rope-mother-told-club-cost.title: The rope-mother told you why the club costs coin
prologue-rope-mother-told-club-cost.plural: The rope-mother told you why the club costs coin

prologue-rope-mother-told-saving.title: The rope-mother told you why nobody saves for their own release
prologue-rope-mother-told-saving.plural: The rope-mother told you why nobody saves for their own release

prologue-rope-mother-told-wants.title: The rope-mother told you what she wants
prologue-rope-mother-told-wants.plural: The rope-mother told you what she wants
prologue-rope-mother-told-wants.description: Hidden: a ferry-boat, twelve coin, and she has four.

prologue-rope-mother-told-why-here.title: The rope-mother told you why she stays outside the walls
prologue-rope-mother-told-why-here.plural: The rope-mother told you why she stays outside the walls

prologue-rope-mother-told-young-man.title: The rope-mother talked about the young man
prologue-rope-mother-told-young-man.plural: The rope-mother talked about the young man

prologue-rumour-reformers.title: Rumour: the reformers did it
prologue-rumour-reformers.description: Some in the crowd say the reformers killed the fleet's binder, to free the dead.

levels.1: The crowd in the camp below the wall, who hate the reformers already.

prologue-sat-with-the-saver.title: Watched over the man who saves
prologue-sat-with-the-saver.plural: Watched over the man who saves
prologue-sat-with-the-saver.description: Hidden: how many times you sat by him while he slept.

prologue-saw-the-column.title: Saw the dead go out to work
prologue-saw-the-column.plural: Saw the dead go out to work

prologue-saw-the-release.title: Saw the burial club release one of its own
prologue-saw-the-release.plural: Saw the burial club release one of its own
prologue-saw-the-release.description: Hidden: you saw the burial club's binder bind and release an old hauler at the fire.

prologue-seen-old-clothes.title: Saw the old-clothes seller
prologue-seen-old-clothes.description: Hidden: the character has walked the hawkers' row, past the old-clothes seller's rope.

prologue-shift-beside-today.title: Worked a shift beside the young man today
prologue-shift-beside-today.plural: Worked a shift beside the young man today

prologue-signed-to-the-company.title: Signed your death to the company
prologue-signed-to-the-company.plural: Signed your death to the company
prologue-signed-to-the-company.description: Hidden: the company holds your claim, and pays for it.

prologue-smuggled-in.title: Came in through the drain
prologue-smuggled-in.description: Hidden: you are inside the walls with no claim.

prologue-sold-the-young-man.title: Sold the young man's body
prologue-sold-the-young-man.description: Hidden: you sold his body to the company. He works for them now.

prologue-struck-from-the-club.title: Struck from the burial club
prologue-struck-from-the-club.description: Hidden: you missed your dues, and the rope-mother struck your knot through. What you paid stays in the box.

prologue-threatened-the-deserters.title: Threatened the deserters
prologue-threatened-the-deserters.description: Hidden: you told the deserters past the last tents that the wardens would like to know where they sleep. They moved their fire.

prologue-told-the-saver-about-the-club.title: Told the man who saves about the burial club
prologue-told-the-saver-about-the-club.plural: Told the man who saves about the burial club

prologue-wardens-felt-the-cold.title: A warden felt the cold in your hands
prologue-wardens-felt-the-cold.plural: A warden felt the cold in your hands
prologue-wardens-felt-the-cold.description: Hidden: a warden at the land gate felt a hedge-binder's cold hands, and remembers the face.

prologue-work-chapel.title: Shown the work with the camp's dead
prologue-work-chapel.plural: Shown the work with the camp's dead
prologue-work-chapel.description: Hidden: Sister Ilse lets you help with the camp's dead at the chapel.

prologue-work-dead-yard.title: Shown the dead-yard shift
prologue-work-dead-yard.description: Hidden: the company takes you on for shifts in its dead-yard.

prologue-work-foraging.title: Shown where the river feeds people
prologue-work-foraging.plural: Shown where the river feeds people
prologue-work-foraging.description: Hidden: you know where to forage along the river.

prologue-work-night-watch.title: Shown the night watch
prologue-work-night-watch.description: Hidden: the fires take you on for the night watch over the camp's dead.

prologue-worked-the-bone-cart.title: Worked the bone-cart
prologue-worked-the-bone-cart.description: Hidden: a recent event. The yard-keeper won't need a hand again for a day or two.

prologue-worked-the-dead-yard.title: Worked a shift in the dead-yard
prologue-worked-the-dead-yard.plural: Worked a shift in the dead-yard
prologue-worked-the-dead-yard.description: Hidden: you have worked in the company's dead-yard, and know your way round it.

prologue-young-man-cared.title: What you did for the young man
prologue-young-man-cared.plural: What you did for the young man
prologue-young-man-cared.description: Hidden: the kinds of care the character gave the young man, 0 to 4: bread, warmth, company, the surgeon.

prologue-young-man-company.title: Kept the young man company
prologue-young-man-company.description: Hidden: talked with him, sat with him, or worked beside him.

prologue-young-man-last-night.title: The young man's last night
prologue-young-man-last-night.description: Hidden: the night after the news.

prologue-young-man-sickness.title: The young man's sickness
prologue-young-man-sickness.description: Hidden: how sick the young man is. 1: a cough. 2: a fever. 3: too weak to get up.

prologue-young-man-surgeon.title: Took the young man to the surgeon
prologue-young-man-surgeon.plural: Took the young man to the surgeon
prologue-young-man-surgeon.description: Hidden: the surgeon refused him: a fever, and no seal.

prologue-young-man-told-cough.title: The young man talked about his cough
prologue-young-man-told-cough.plural: The young man talked about his cough

prologue-young-man-told-farms.title: The young man told you where he is from
prologue-young-man-told-farms.plural: The young man told you where he is from

prologue-young-man-told-signing.title: The young man told you he means to sign
prologue-young-man-told-signing.plural: The young man told you he means to sign
prologue-young-man-told-signing.description: Hidden: he asked you to work a shift in the dead-yard beside him.

prologue-young-man-under-your-coat.title: Put your coat over the young man on his last night
prologue-young-man-under-your-coat.plural: Put your coat over the young man on his last night

provisions.title: Provisions
provisions.description: Food enough for the road, or not.

rags.title: What you walked out in
rags.description: Torn, stained, and not all of it yours.

regard-binder.title: The binder at the chapel
regard-binder.description: How [who:regard-binder] feels about you, from 0 to 10. The higher it is, the more she will do for you.

levels.0: A young woman with grey hair and cold hands.
levels.1: Looks up when you sit down.
levels.2: Looks for you in the line.
levels.3: Answers you straight, hands over the coals.
levels.4: Almost smiles when you come in.
levels.5: Trusts you.
levels.8: Would take a cost for you.

regard-binder.changeUp: [who:regard-binder] thinks better of you. Regard [qb:regard-binder] of 10: [q:regard-binder]
regard-binder.changeDown: [who:regard-binder] thinks less of you. Regard [qb:regard-binder] of 10: [q:regard-binder]

regard-rope-mother.title: The old woman at the haulers' fire
regard-rope-mother.plural: The old woman at the haulers' fire
regard-rope-mother.description: How [who:regard-rope-mother] feels about you, from 0 to 10. The higher it is, the more she will do for you: vouch for you, tell you things, hide you.

levels.0: One more mouth at the fire.
levels.2: Saves you a place at the fire.
levels.3: Talks to you while she works.
levels.4: Gives you the thick end of the pot.
levels.5: Would vouch for you.
levels.6: Speaks of you as one of ours.
levels.7: Waits up when you are late.

regard-rope-mother.changeUp: [who:regard-rope-mother] thinks better of you. Regard [qb:regard-rope-mother] of 10: [q:regard-rope-mother]
regard-rope-mother.changeDown: [who:regard-rope-mother] thinks less of you. Regard [qb:regard-rope-mother] of 10: [q:regard-rope-mother]

regard-yard-keeper.title: The yard-keeper at the back gate
regard-yard-keeper.plural: The yard-keeper at the back gate
regard-yard-keeper.description: How [who:regard-yard-keeper] feels about you, from 0 to 10.

levels.0: A man with a cloth over his face, who sews up the dead.
levels.1: Hands you the lantern without asking.

regard-yard-keeper.changeUp: [who:regard-yard-keeper] thinks better of you. Regard [qb:regard-yard-keeper] of 10: [q:regard-yard-keeper]
regard-yard-keeper.changeDown: [who:regard-yard-keeper] thinks less of you. Regard [qb:regard-yard-keeper] of 10: [q:regard-yard-keeper]

rested.title: Rested
rested.description: How clear your head is. Choices that need a clear head test it. It falls as Sleepiness rises; sleep restores it.

levels.5: Awake enough.

rites.title: Rites
rites.description: Doctrine, binding, the dead, heresy, how the church thinks.

levels.1: Knows the prayers by rote and no more.
levels.2: Knows the prayers, and what each one is for.
levels.3: Knows what the rites cost, and who pays.
levels.4: Understands what the church is really doing.
levels.5: Hears what a priest means under what he says.
levels.6: Can argue a point of doctrine, if the priest is tired.
levels.7: Could argue doctrine with a priest.

road-boots.title: Road boots
road-boots.description: Cracked across the toes, and caked to the ankle with the road.

road-breeches.title: Road breeches
road-breeches.description: Grey with dust to the knee, and patched where the patches wore through.

road-shirt.title: A road shirt
road-shirt.description: Linen gone the colour of the road. It has been slept in more nights than you can count.

rose-water.title: A phial of rose water
rose-water.description: A dab at the throat and wrists leaves a faint smell of roses.

levels.2: Male.

shaken.title: Shaken
shaken.description: Rattled by what you've just seen or done. Hard to sleep while it lasts.

levels.1: Shaken. Your nerve is not what it was, for now.

shield.title: Shield
shield.description: A temperament. You stand between danger and other people.
shield.changeUp: You put yourself between harm and someone else. Shield grows to [qb:shield]. [Temperaments rise at moments like this one. Each opens choices that only that kind of person would see.]

levels.2: Loads, aims and fires, slowly.
levels.3: Hits what you aim at, if it is large.
levels.5: Loads fast, and hits what you aim at.
levels.6: Hits what you aim at, mostly.

sickness.title: Sickness
sickness.description: Fever, plague, the slow kind of dying. A wound left to fester brings it on, and a surgeon wants to know who holds your death before he treats it. Makes every test harder.

levels.5: Very sick. This could kill you.
levels.6: Barely conscious. One more turn will kill you.

sleepiness.title: Sleepiness
sleepiness.description: How long you have been awake. Sleep clears it. The more tired you are, the lower your Rested, and the harder any test that needs a clear head.

levels.2: Awake enough.
levels.5: Tired. A bed would be welcome.

soldiers-clothes.title: A soldier's jacket
soldiers-clothes.description: Slashed sleeves, faded colours. It still shouts across a field.

style.title: Style
style.description: Your style is the way you wear your clothes. You choose a style at a place where you can change clothes. You can choose a style only when your clothes have [c:style-points] points of that style.

levels.2: Plain as a Nail
levels.5: Gilt to the Neck

style-foreign.title: Foreign Cut
style-foreign.description: Foreign Cut is a style of clothes cut and dyed in a foreign way. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-gilt.title: Gilt to the Neck
style-gilt.description: Gilt to the Neck is a style of gold, silver and as much shine as possible. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-graveside.title: Graveside
style-graveside.description: Graveside is a style of black clothes and mourning jewellery. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-laces.title: Loose Laces
style-laces.description: Loose Laces is a style of clothes worn a little loose, with more skin on show. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-plain.title: Plain as a Nail
style-plain.description: Plain as a Nail is a style of plain clothes with no decoration. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-road.title: Road Rags
style-road.description: Road Rags is a style of patched clothes worn in layers, like a traveller. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-rustic.title: Rustic
style-rustic.description: Rustic is a style of sturdy wool and plain country clothes. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-silk.title: Silk and Starch
style-silk.description: Silk and Starch is a style of fine, clean clothes that are kept neat. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-swagger.title: Swagger
style-swagger.description: Swagger is a style of bold clothes that are made to be noticed. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

style-sweat.title: Sweat and Rust
style-sweat.description: Sweat and Rust is a style of rough, scuffed leather and iron. Each worn item can add points to a style. When your clothes have [c:style-points] points of this style, you can choose this style at a place where you can change clothes.

surgeon.title: The surgeon
surgeon.description: Hidden: the surgeon by the road, by name once he gives it.

suspicion.title: Suspicion
suspicion.description: What the wardens and informers know, or think they know, about you.

levels.5: You are being watched.
levels.7: The wardens are coming for you.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: How cold it is, wherever you are.

levels.2: Cool.

tongue.title: Tongue
tongue.description: A temperament. You talk, bargain and lie your way through.
tongue.changeUp: You talked your way to what you wanted. Tongue grows to [qb:tongue]. [Temperaments rise at moments like this one. Each opens choices that only that kind of person would see.]

trait.title: Trait
trait.description: The kind of person the character is, all game.

levels.2: Doubter.
levels.5: Proud.

warmth.title: Warmth
warmth.description: How well what you're wearing holds the cold off.

levels.2: Adequate.

weapon-boat-hook.title: A boat-hook
weapon-boat-hook.description: A hauler's pole with an iron hook. Keeps the risen at arm's length, and then some.

weapon-cudgel.title: A cudgel
weapon-cudgel.description: Oak, with iron round the end. It does for a skull.

weapon-hanger.title: A soldier's short sword
weapon-hanger.description: Heavy and plain, from the edge wars, made for close work in a press.

weapon-knife.title: A knife
weapon-knife.description: Long enough for a throat, short enough for a sleeve.

weapon-pistol.title: A wheel-lock pistol
weapon-pistol.description: Unloaded. Powder costs more than bread this year.

wool-cap.title: A wool cap
wool-cap.description: Grey wool, mended at the top. It smells of someone else's hair.

wounds.title: Wounds
wounds.description: Cuts, breaks, and the pain of them. A wound wants tending, or it festers. Thieves pick out the hurt, and strangers offer help at a price. A surgeon wants to know who holds your death before he touches a bad one. Makes Brawn, Arms and Shot tests harder.

levels.3: Hurting, where people can see it.
levels.5: Badly hurt. Another blow could finish you.
levels.6: Barely standing. One more wound will kill you.

wounds-cutpurse-lying-low.title: The cutpurse lies low
wounds-cutpurse-lying-low.description: Hidden: a recent event. The boy who works the crush between the tents keeps away from you for a while.

wounds-festering.title: A wound gone bad
wounds-festering.description: Hidden: a wound that festers. Cleaning it out, a surgeon or the yard-keeper ends it.

wounds-heard-of-the-surgeon.title: Heard of the surgeon
wounds-heard-of-the-surgeon.description: Hidden: people in the camp told you of the surgeon's awning by the road.

wounds-needle.title: The Yard-Keeper's Needle
wounds-needle.description: Someone to stitch a wound that the surgeon won't touch.

levels.1: Turned away at the surgeon's awning: no seal. He says the yard-keeper behind the company tent sews anything, after the dead come in at Vespers.
levels.2: The yard-keeper at the company's back gate mends the living too, for a price.

next.1: Go round behind the company tent to the yard's back gate, after the dead come in at Vespers.

wounds-needle-name-in-the-book.title: The yard-keeper wrote your name in his book
wounds-needle-name-in-the-book.plural: The yard-keeper wrote your name in his book
wounds-needle-name-in-the-book.description: Hidden: the yard-keeper stitched you for nothing, and wrote your name in his book.

wounds-needle-worked-for-him.title: Held the yard-keeper's lantern for pay
wounds-needle-worked-for-him.plural: Held the yard-keeper's lantern for pay
wounds-needle-worked-for-him.description: Hidden: you have worked a night for the yard-keeper.

young-man.title: The young man with the cough
young-man.plural: The young man with the cough
young-man.description: Hidden: the young man from the farms, by name once he gives it.

a-claim-for-sale.title: A Claim for Sale
a-claim-for-sale.intro: A man sits at the side of the road with a board across his knees, and a price chalked on it. "For me," he says, when you stop. "When I go. I'll wear your sign, and you come for me before I get up again. The yard pays six for one that walks." He coughs into his sleeve. "[c:claim-for-sale-price] coin. Today."

branches.title: Pay him, and hold his death
branches.description: Pay him what he asks, and hold his death.

success.title: A disc of lead
success.description: He has a disc of lead ready, already holed for a cord. You scratch your sign into it with his nail, and he hangs it round his neck, and that's all it takes to hold a man's death. "Don't be long," he says, "when it comes."{if [q:binder] > 0} Your cold fingers know exactly what he'll be worth.{/if}

branches.title: Give him a coin, and keep your sign
branches.description: Give him a coin, and keep your sign to yourself.

success.title: Charity
success.description: He takes the coin, bites it, and puts it away. "Charity," he says, as if it's a word for something that goes off. He wipes the price off his board with his sleeve, and chalks it up again, the same.{if [q:trait] == 3} You'd give him more, if you had more.{/if}

branches.title: Walk on
branches.description: Walk on down the road. Someone will buy.

success.title: Lower, and lower
success.description: You walk on, further down. Behind you he calls his price again, lower, and then lower still, until you can't hear him.

a-closer-look.title: A Closer Look
a-closer-look.intro: The water settles again.{if [q:features-picked] >= 1} You look a while longer.{/if} What else does it show you?

branches.title: Tall
branches.description: Tall: a head over most crowds.
branches.hoverText: Presence +1. People remember you.

success.title: Tall
success.description: Even kneeling, you're a head over the woman with the bucket. In a crowd, you're the one people point to. And remember.

branches.title: Slight
branches.description: Slight: small, and lightly made.
branches.hoverText: Guile +1, Brawn -1. Overlooked, and not trusted with heavy work.

success.title: Slight
success.description: A narrow face on a narrow frame. People look past you, and nobody picks you for heavy work. Some days that's a mercy.

branches.title: Broad and heavy
branches.description: Broad and heavy: built like a barrel, with the shoulders to match.
branches.hoverText: Brawn +1. Hunger comes faster.

success.title: Broad and heavy
success.description: Your shoulders fill the water from bank to bank. Work gangs want a back like yours, and people think twice. You eat like two of them, too.

branches.title: Pox-scarred
branches.description: Pox-scarred: a face pitted all over by an old sickness.
branches.hoverText: No skill changes. Some think you can't catch it twice; some think you carry it.

success.title: Pox-scarred
success.description: Pitted from cheek to brow, from the pox that didn't kill you. The woman with the bucket moves along the bank. Some think you can't catch it twice. Some think you carry it still.

branches.title: Striking
branches.description: Striking: a face people turn round to look at again.
branches.hoverText: Presence +1. Doors open, and so does unwanted attention.

success.title: Striking
success.description: The woman with the bucket turns round to look at you again. People do. Doors open for a face like that, and not all looking is friendly.

branches.title: Forgettable face
branches.description: A forgettable face: nobody can describe it an hour later.
branches.hoverText: No skill changes. Witnesses argue about what you looked like.

success.title: Forgettable face
success.description: A face like any other face. You look away, and even you can't quite call it back. Nor will anyone else.

branches.title: Maimed hand
branches.description: A maimed hand: two fingers gone, long healed.
branches.hoverText: Arms -1. Veterans and beggars take you for one of their own.

success.title: Maimed hand
success.description: Two fingers gone from the hand you dip in the water, long healed. Fine work comes hard. Old soldiers and beggars nod at that hand like a password.

branches.title: Grey too young
branches.description: Grey too young: your hair went before its time.
branches.hoverText: No skill changes. People assume you've seen something, and old folk talk to you.

success.title: Grey too young
success.description: Grey at the temples, and too soon. People look at your hair, then at your face, and decide you've seen something. Old folk tell you things.

branches.title: Soft hands
branches.description: Soft hands: plainly never a day's hard work.
branches.hoverText: No skill changes. You look better-off. Labourers don't trust you.

success.title: Soft hands
success.description: Your hands are white in the brown water, and soft. Labourers see them before they see your face, and spit.

branches.title: A limp
branches.description: A limp: one leg drags, a little, every step.
branches.hoverText: No skill changes. Slower on the road and in flight. Pitied, or picked on.

success.title: A limp
success.description: Even kneeling, you favour the bad leg, as you always do. It drags a little, every step. You'll never outrun anyone. Some people pity that. Some push.

branches.title: That's all it shows
branches.description: That's all it shows. That's all anyone will see.

success.title: Downstream
success.description: You stand up, and the river takes your face away downstream.

a-hand-for-the-bone-cart.title: A Hand for the Bone-Cart
a-hand-for-the-bone-cart.intro:
A cart at the dead-yard's back gate, and a yard-keeper with a cloth tied over his face. One of his dead has stopped. It sat down in the mud an hour since, and won't get up for any bell. Worn out.

"Need a hand," he says. "Pays."

branches.title: Lift it onto the cart
branches.description: Take it under the arms and lift it onto the cart.

success.title: Three coin, and wet sleeves
success.description: It's lighter than it looks, and wet all through. You get it up onto the bones already in the cart, and it lies there with its eyes open, finished at last by nothing but wear. Three coin, and your sleeves are soaked to the elbow.

failure.title: It comes apart
failure.description: Your back and shoulders take the whole weight, and they'll be the stronger for it. Then the arm comes away in your hands, and you sit down hard in the mud, holding it. The yard-keeper gets the rest up himself, and keeps his coin.

branches.title: Hold the horse
branches.description: Hold the horse and steady the cart while he does the lifting.

success.title: One coin
success.description: The horse hates the smell of the dead, and stamps in its harness. You talk to it while he works. One coin, and he tells you the cart goes to the bone-mill on the rapids. "Everything goes somewhere," he says.

a-hand-in-your-coat.title: A Hand in Your Coat
a-hand-in-your-coat.intro: In the crush between the tents, a hand slides into your coat, light as a cat, and closes on your purse. You look down. A boy of ten or twelve looks back up at you, and doesn't let go{if [q:wounds] >= 3}. He has watched you nurse that wound all day, and picked you for slow{/if}{if [q:wounds] < 3 && [q:appearance] >= 3}. Your good clothes picked you out for him{/if}.

branches.title: Grab his wrist
branches.description: Grab his wrist before he's away.

success.title: Teeth
success.description: You catch his wrist, and he sinks his teeth into your hand, to the bone. You don't let go. He drops the purse, wrenches free and is gone between the tents, and you stand there bleeding, with your coin.

failure.title: Gone, with nothing
failure.description: You throw your whole weight at him, and your arms will be the stronger for it. He's quicker. He lets go of the purse to twist free, and he's under a cart and gone, with nothing of yours.

failure.title: His knife
failure.description: You throw your whole weight at him, and your arms will be the stronger for it. You get a fistful of his collar. Then there's a knife in his other hand, and it goes into you, and you're down in the mud with your hand pressed to the place. He's gone. Your purse lies in the mud beside you, where he let go of it for the knife. Nobody stops. Somebody steps over you.

branches.title: Turn on him armed
branches.description: Show him {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if}. He's only a boy. He'll let go.

success.title: Empty-handed
success.description: He takes one look at what's in your hand and lets go of the purse as if it burned him, and he's gone between the tents. Nobody round you says a word. In this crush, everyone keeps a hand on their own.

failure.title: Gone into the crowd
failure.description: Your grip is surer for it, and your arm quicker. He is quicker still: he lets go of the purse, and he's through a gap between two carts and gone, with nothing of yours.

failure.title: A knife of his own
failure.description: Your grip is surer for it, and your arm quicker. He doesn't run. He has a knife of his own, and he has used it before: under your guard, in, and out. You go down in the mud. When you can look up, he's gone, and your purse lies in the mud by your hand, where he let go of it.

branches.title: Give him a coin to be rid of him
branches.description: Give him a coin, and he'll take his hand out of your coat. It's only coin, and you can count his ribs through his shirt.

success.title: One coin
success.description: You put a coin in the hand that's in your coat. He looks at it, then at you, and he's gone between the tents in a breath. Somewhere a woman shouts at him, and then at you, for paying him.

a-new-price.title: A New Price
a-new-price.intro: The baker has wiped his board and chalked up a new price.{if [q:origin] == 1} You know what a sack of flour fetched at harvest. Not this.{/if} "No fleet, no flour," he says, before anyone can ask. At the front, a woman counts her coins into her palm twice, and comes up one short. The baker waits. So does everyone behind her.

branches.title: Put in the coin she's short
branches.description: Reach past her, and put the coin she's short on the board.

success.title: Somebody saw
success.description:
The baker takes it without a word. The woman takes her loaf the same way, and goes. She doesn't look back.

[who:regard-rope-mother] was three places behind you in the crowd. At the fire that night she gives you the first bowl, and says nothing about why.

branches.title: Buy two loaves before it goes up again
branches.description: Buy two loaves now, at [c:bread-price] coin, before he chalks it up again.

success.title: At the new price
success.description: The baker counts your coin twice, as if it might be short too. Two dark loaves, warm through the cloth. Behind you, the woman is still standing there, one coin short.

branches.title: Ask him what the fleet has to do with yesterday's flour
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 9}You're already shouting before you've decided to. Ask him what a fleet on the river has to do with flour he baked yesterday.{else}Ask him, loud enough for the crowd, what a fleet on the river has to do with flour he baked yesterday.{/if}

success.title: Yesterday's price
success.description:
The crowd takes it up. "Yesterday's flour!" Somebody bangs on his board. The baker looks at the crowd, then at the wardens up the road, and sells the last of yesterday's bake at yesterday's price, to shut you all up. One loaf each, and quickly.

"I'll remember you," he says, as he takes your coin.

failure.title: The crowd laughs
failure.description: You learn how to pitch your voice over a crowd. You learn it a moment too late. "Flour's dear, bread's dear," the baker says, to the crowd, not to you. "Ask the fleet." They laugh, and you're the joke, and by the time they've stopped you've lost your place. No bread for you today.

branches.title: Take a loaf while he's arguing
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 6}Nobody is watching the end of the board. Bread is bread, and it's never cost him what he's asking. Take a loaf while he's busy.{else}Nobody is watching the end of the board. Take a loaf while he's busy with the crowd.{/if}

success.title: Under your coat
success.description: A loaf under your coat, warm against your ribs, and you're out of the crowd before he looks round. Your heart doesn't slow down until you're back at the fire.

failure.title: Thief
failure.description: Your fingers are quicker for the try; next time nobody will see them. This time the baker's boy does. He grabs your wrist and yells "Thief!" loud enough to carry. You twist free and lose yourself in the crowd. But up the road a warden has turned his head, and seen your face.

a-night-in-the-city.title: A Night in the City
a-night-in-the-city.intro: All night the bells, every hour, and the handbells answering. Once, a breaking somewhere far off, or a fire: shouting, and then nothing.

branches.title: Wake
branches.description: Wake, stiff, in the porch.

success.title: Bells
success.description: Prime. The dead go out to the mills, and the bread queue is longer than yesterday.

a-place-by-the-fire.title: A Place by the Fire
a-place-by-the-fire.intro:
The camp smells of wet ash and tanneries. Downwind is the dead-yard: a long fence, lanterns, and a sound like cattle settling, except cattle breathe.

You find room at a fire of haulers. An old woman with forearms like rope stirs a pot and hands round the bowls. Beside you, a young man from the farms coughs into his sleeve and grins as if it's nothing. Across the road a company crier calls for people to sign on, and his eye keeps coming back to the young man. Up by the gate, a chapel bell rings once, for somebody.

Then a drover brings a column of dead in from the fields, ringing his handbell, and the whole fire goes quiet until they've passed.

branches.title: Take the bowl she holds out
branches.description: Take the bowl she holds out, and sit down with them.

success.title: Turned back
success.description:
The stew is thin and hot, and nobody asks your business. "Turned back?" says the old woman. "Most are, the first time. [who:regard-rope-mother]." She points the ladle along the log. "That's [who:young-man]. He's from the farms. Thinks everything's funny."

"Not everything," he says, and coughs. "Most things."

An old man with a face as brown and creased as an old glove passes you the salt without being asked. Then he wipes his bowl with his thumb, shoulders a shovel, and goes off down toward the dead-yard. "Mucking out," the young man says. "For the company. Half of them do, now."

a-room-behind-the-chapel.title: A Room Behind the Chapel
a-room-behind-the-chapel.intro: [who:regard-binder] is on the river steps, rinsing out her basin, her hands red and blue from the water. She sees you and stops. "You're still sleeping on the ground," she says. It isn't a question. "I've a room behind the chapel. It's the size of a cupboard, and the stove smokes. There's floor enough for two."

branches.title: Say yes
branches.description: Say yes, before she thinks better of it, and thank her.

success.title: The latch is up
success.description: "Don't thank me till you've smelled the stove." She takes you up past the line, to a low door in the wall behind her table. A room the size of a cupboard: a cot, a stove, a shelf of blank seals, and a straw mattress rolled up in the corner. "After Compline the line's gone. Come then. Don't wake me."

branches.title: Tell her you've slept on worse floors
branches.description: Tell her you've slept on worse floors, and never in better company.

success.title: You haven't heard me snore
success.description: She looks at you a moment, and something in her face warms that the fire pan never reaches. "You haven't heard me snore," she says, and hitches the basin up on her hip. "Come after Compline. I'll leave the latch up, and we'll see how long the company lasts." She goes on up the steps, and doesn't look back. Not quite.

branches.title: Tell her you'll manage on the ground
branches.description: Tell her you'll manage on the ground. Everyone else does.

success.title: The ground's free
success.description: She shrugs, the way the camp shrugs at everything. "The ground's free," she says. "So's my floor. The latch is up after Compline, if the ground gets any harder." She goes on up the steps with her basin.

a-share-in-the-far-shore.title: Shares in the Morning Star
a-share-in-the-far-shore.intro:
A woman in a blue coat stands on a barrel and sings it out over the camp: "A land across the sea! No dead, no war, no hunger, no debt! Shares in the *Morning Star*, sailing on the spring tide!"

She holds up printed papers. Most people walk past her. One or two stop.

branches.title: Buy a share
branches.description: Buy a share. One coin.

success.title: A ship, a shore, a sun
success.description: The paper is good and the printing better: a ship, a shore, a sun. "Your name goes on the list," she says, "when the ship is full." You fold it small and keep it next to your skin. For the first time in weeks, you catch yourself thinking about spring.

branches.title: Ask when she sails
branches.description: Ask her when the ship sails.

success.title: When she's full
success.description: "On the spring tide," she says, beaming, "when she's full." Which spring, she doesn't say. She's singing again, over your head.

branches.title: Laugh at her
branches.description: Laugh at her, out loud.

success.title: Heard worse
success.description: You laugh, and a few people in the queue laugh with you. She sings over all of you; she's heard worse. By the barrel, a man folds his share away carefully, as if you might take it from him.

a-weeks-grace.title: A Week's Grace
a-weeks-grace.intro:
At the last fire, by the mill race, a woman gets up before you reach her, and stays standing. Her hands are wrapped in rags to the wrist. "The wheel's stopped till they mend it," she says. "A week, and I'll pay both." She doesn't look at [who:regard-rope-mother]. She looks at you, and the box.

[who:regard-rope-mother] holds the charcoal over the book, and waits. Then she looks at you too. "You carried it," she says. "You say."

branches.title: Tell her she has a week
branches.description: Tell the woman she has a week.

success.title: Lighter
success.description: [who:regard-rope-mother] writes something small beside the woman's name, and you carry the box back a little lighter than it should be. She says nothing all the way. At the haulers' fire she takes the box from you and weighs it in her hands. "I'll remember that," she says. Then she moves along her coil to make room for you.

branches.title: Tell her the box can't wait
branches.description: Tell the woman the box can't wait.

success.title: A line through her name
success.description: [who:regard-rope-mother] draws a line through the woman's name, and holds out her hand. The woman takes the seal from her neck and gives it up, and sits down. Nobody at the mill fire says a word to you, and every one of them looks at your face. At the haulers' fire [who:regard-rope-mother] takes the box back, and moves along her coil to make room for you. "That's the rule," she says. "Somebody has to say it."

all-at-once.title: All at Once
all-at-once.intro: Four men on their feet, and the one with his hand in his coat has taken it out. A knife, held low, the way soldiers are taught. "Say it again," he says.

branches.title: Fight them armed
branches.description: Put your back to the wall and {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if} between you and them, and show them you know how to use it.

success.title: Nobody wants to be first
success.description: The first one in gets a cut across the arm for his trouble, and you get his elbow in your face. Then they look at each other. Nobody wants to be next. In the end they kick out their fire and go, cursing you over their shoulders.

failure.title: Soldiers
failure.description: You learn more in that minute than in a month of practice. But they were soldiers, and there are four of them. When they're done, they take half your coin, kick out their fire and go, and you lie by the ashes until you can stand.

branches.title: Fight them with your fists
branches.description: Get your back to the wall, raise your fists, and make the first one sorry.

success.title: Back to the wall
success.description: The first one in catches your fist on the nose, and the second catches the wall when you step aside. They could finish it, four to one. They look at each other, and decide it isn't worth the noise, and go, kicking out their fire as they leave.

failure.title: By the ashes
failure.description: Every blow you trade hardens your arms a little. It doesn't help much against four men who learned to fight in a war. When they're done, they take half your coin and leave you by the ashes of their fire, and it's a long time before you can stand.

branches.title: Swear you saw nothing
branches.description: Swear you saw nothing, and empty your purse to prove it.

success.title: Pushed back with a boot
success.description: You tip your purse out onto their blanket. They take half, and push the rest back at you with a boot. "You didn't see us," the one with the knife says again, and this time you agree. By dark their fire will be somewhere else.

another-night-behind-the-chapel.title: Another Night Behind the Chapel
another-night-behind-the-chapel.intro:
A night on the mattress by [who:regard-binder]'s stove: the stove ticking as it cools, and her breathing, slow and even, a few feet away.{if [q:prologue] == 3}

At first light someone hammers on the chapel door: a hauler's girl, out of breath. "[who:regard-rope-mother] wants you at the fire," she says. She won't say why.{/if}

branches.title: Wake
branches.description: {if [q:prologue] == 3}Pull your boots on, and go.{else}Wake, warm, to another day outside the walls.{/if}

success.title: Already at her table
success.description: {if [q:prologue] == 3}[who:regard-binder] is already at her table. She looks at your face, and doesn't ask. "Go on," she says. "I'll be here."{else}Grey morning. She's already at her table, and the line's already at the door.{/if}

another-night-below-the-wall.title: Another Night Below the Wall
another-night-below-the-wall.intro: {if [q:prologue] <= 2}Another night on the ground below the wall. The river, the dead-yard's lanterns, and two logs down, [who:young-man]'s cough, on and off till morning.{/if}{if [q:prologue] == 3}Another night on the ground below the wall. The river, the dead-yard's lanterns, and [who:young-man]'s cough, two logs down. Some time in the small hours it stops. You're too tired to wonder why.{/if}{if [q:prologue] >= 4}Another night on the ground below the wall. The river, the dead-yard's lanterns, and somewhere a cough that isn't [who:young-man]'s, because his has stopped.{/if}

branches.title: Wake
branches.description: Wake, cold, to another day outside.

success.title: Grey morning
success.description: Grey morning. Up at the gate, the wardens are taking down the bar.

before-he-rises.title: Before He Rises
before-he-rises.intro:
News gets round a camp fast. The company man is already strolling over with his ledger under his arm. Somebody has run for the chapel. The haulers stand round with their thumbs in their belts, looking at the old woman. And down the road come two wardens, in no hurry.

Everybody here has a use for what's under that blanket.

branches.title: Meet the company man
branches.description: Meet the company man halfway. He was nobody's, so he may as well be yours to sell.

success.title: Six coin
success.description:
"Next of kin?" says the company man, writing. "Near enough," you say. Six coin.

Two yard hands carry [who:young-man] off on a door. By noon he'll be standing in a row with a nail in his skull. [who:regard-rope-mother] turns her back on you, and keeps it turned.

branches.title: Carry him to the chapel
branches.description: Carry him up to the chapel. "She'll do him for nothing," says [who:regard-rope-mother]. "Nothing to you, I mean. She pays for it herself, out of her own warmth."
branches.hoverText: The chapel binder asks no coin of paupers. The binding costs her, not you: the Binder's Chill, in her own body.

success.title: At her cost
success.description:
The binder in grey kneels by him on the chapel floor. The rite is short. She binds him with a bare nail, and he opens his eyes, and in the same breath she draws it out again, and he closes them for good.

She sits back on her heels and stays there, blowing on her hands. She shakes her head before you can ask what you owe. "[who:regard-binder]," she says, when she can. "You owe nothing. I pay for these myself. He's nobody's now."

branches.title: Carry him to the chapel
branches.description: Carry him up to [who:regard-binder]. "She'll do him for nothing," says [who:regard-rope-mother]. "Nothing to you. She pays for it herself, out of her own warmth."
branches.hoverText: The chapel binder asks no coin of paupers. The binding costs her, not you: the Binder's Chill, in her own body.

success.title: At her cost
success.description:
[who:regard-binder] gets up from her table when she sees what you're carrying, and kneels by him on the chapel floor. The rite is short. She binds him with a bare nail, and he opens his eyes, and in the same breath she draws it out again, and he closes them for good.

She stays on her knees a while, blowing on her hands. When you start to ask what you owe, she shakes her head. "Nothing. I pay for these myself," she says. "He's nobody's now."

branches.title: Burn him
branches.description: Help the haulers build a fire, and burn him before anyone can stop it.
branches.hoverText: Burning a body destroys someone's claim. The law calls it theft, and the church calls it heresy.

success.title: Quick and bright
success.description:
Rope, tar, every stick in the camp. The haulers work fast and say nothing. The company man shouts about theft. The wardens come at a run when they see the smoke, too late. [who:young-man] goes up quick and bright, and nobody will ever work him.

A warden looks at you for a long time, and writes in a little book.

branches.title: Bind him yourself
branches.description: Kneel, and bind him yourself. You know how. Nobody here needs to know you know.
branches.hoverText: Binding costs you: the Binder's Chill. You will hold his binding, and he will wait for you.

success.title: He waits
success.description:
Your hands on his face. The words under your breath. {if [q:keepsake-nail] > 0}Not your sister's nail, the pulled one in your kit: that one stays. A plain nail from the heel of your boot, kept for a day like this.{else}The nail from the heel of your boot.{/if} The cold goes into you like a river.

When you take your hands away, [who:young-man] sits up, and waits. Just waits, his eyes on you. The haulers step back. [who:regard-rope-mother] doesn't. She looks at you as if she's never seen you before.

branches.title: Leave him to the wardens
branches.description: Leave him. It isn't yours to decide, and he isn't your kin.

success.title: The law, for the unclaimed
success.description:
The wardens take him in the end, because nobody else will. They don't carry him far: to the ditch by the road, where one of them takes his head off with a spade, neatly, like a man cutting turf. It's the law, for the unclaimed.

You watched. [who:regard-rope-mother] watched you watch.

behind-the-canvas.title: Behind the Canvas
behind-the-canvas.intro:
Two hand-carts with a strip of sailcloth tied between them, out of the wind and out of sight. Somebody's shirt hangs drying on a rope.

[Here you can change everything you wear, in the Kit tab.]

branches.title: Graveside
branches.description: Wear black clothes, like a mourner.

success.title: Graveside
success.description: You are dressed in black, like a mourner.

branches.title: Plain as a Nail
branches.description: Wear plain clothes with no decoration.

success.title: Plain as a Nail
success.description: You are dressed in plain clothes, with nothing to catch the eye.

branches.title: Swagger
branches.description: Wear your clothes boldly, and walk with your chin high.

success.title: Swagger
success.description: You hold your chin high, and you walk with a swagger.

branches.title: Silk and Starch
branches.description: Wear your cleanest clothes, and keep every fold neat.

success.title: Silk and Starch
success.description: Your collar is clean, and every fold is neat.

branches.title: Gilt to the Neck
branches.description: Wear every shiny thing you own at the same time.

success.title: Gilt to the Neck
success.description: You wear your gold and silver where everyone can see it.

branches.title: Rustic
branches.description: Wear sturdy wool clothes, like a farmer.

success.title: Rustic
success.description: You are dressed in sturdy wool clothes, like someone from a farm.

branches.title: Road Rags
branches.description: Wear your patched clothes in layers, like a traveller.

success.title: Road Rags
success.description: You are dressed in patched layers, like someone who has walked a long way.

branches.title: Sweat and Rust
branches.description: Wear rough leather and iron.

success.title: Sweat and Rust
success.description: You are dressed in rough, scuffed leather and iron.

branches.title: Loose Laces
branches.description: Wear your clothes a little loose, with more skin on show.

success.title: Loose Laces
success.description: Your clothes hang a little loose, and show more skin than usual.

branches.title: Foreign Cut
branches.description: Wear clothes cut and dyed in a foreign way.

success.title: Foreign Cut
success.description: You are dressed in clothes that are cut and dyed in a foreign way.

branches.title: Done
branches.description: Back to the fire.

success.title: Back to the fire
success.description: You come out from behind the canvas.

behind-the-chapel.title: Behind the Chapel
behind-the-chapel.intro:
Her cot creaks when she turns over. Once in the night she gets up to bank the stove, and steps over you in the dark as if she has done it for years. Her breathing, slow and even, a few feet away. You wake warm.{if [q:prologue] == 3}

At first light someone hammers on the chapel door: a hauler's girl, out of breath. "[who:regard-rope-mother] wants you at the fire," she says. She won't say why.{/if}

branches.title: Wake
branches.description: {if [q:prologue] == 3}Pull your boots on, and go with the girl.{else}Roll up the mattress, and get up.{/if}

success.title: The line starts at Prime
success.description: {if [q:prologue] == 3}[who:regard-binder] is up already, pinning her hood. She looks at your face, and doesn't ask. "Go," she says. "I'll be here after."{else}She's up before you, pinning her hood by the light of the stove. "Mattress goes in the corner," she says. "The line starts at Prime."{/if}

branches.title: Tell her she talks in her sleep
branches.description: Tell her she talks in her sleep.

success.title: Worth answering
success.description: She stops with the pin half through her hood. "Then you were listening," she says. "That's worse." At the door she looks back at you, still on her floor. "If I say anything worth hearing, answer me. It's lonely work, talking to the dead all day."

bread-at-a-price.title: Bread at a Price
bread-at-a-price.intro:
Warm bread, somewhere close: you smell it before you see the baker's cart at the edge of the camp, and the crowd round it. The baker shouts a price, then shouts it again, higher.{if [q:crisis-bread-dear] > 0} His board has been chalked over twice since you came.{/if}

"The fleet's late," he says, to anyone who complains. "Want it cheaper? Walk down to the ford and fetch it."

branches.title: Buy two loaves
branches.description: {if [q:crisis-bread-dear] > 0}Pay [c:bread-price] coin for two loaves: four times what bread should cost.{else}Pay [c:bread-price] coin for two loaves: three times what bread should cost.{/if}

success.title: Still warm
success.description: Two dark loaves, still warm. You carry them back through the crowd held against you, like something alive.

branches.title: Buy two, and share one
branches.description: Buy two, and take one back to the haulers' pot.

success.title: Into the pot
success.description: [who:regard-rope-mother] breaks your loaf into the pot without a word, and the whole fire eats. Later she gives you the heel of it, with the nod she gives her own people.

branches.title: Go without
branches.description: Go without. Not at that price.

success.title: Not at that price
success.description: Your belly argues with you for hours. The baker sells out anyway, before the next bell.

cornered.title: Cornered
cornered.intro: Three of them now, close enough to smell, and nobody coming out of the tents. The thin one holds out his hand, palm up. "Purse," he says, as if he were asking the time.

branches.title: Fight them armed
branches.description: Go for the thin one with {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if}, before the other two close in.

success.title: Three men scattering
success.description: Somebody's fist finds your ribs. Then your blow finds somebody's arm, and they've had enough: three men scattering between the tents, one of them bleeding. You keep your purse, and your ribs will tell you about it tomorrow.

failure.title: A knife of his own
failure.description: Your arm finds the rhythm of it, and it will remember. But three is too many. One of them pins your arm, and the thin one has a knife of his own. When you can get up, they're gone, and so is half your coin.

branches.title: Fight them with your fists
branches.description: Hit the thin one first, before he expects it, and keep hitting.

success.title: More trouble than it's worth
success.description: He doesn't expect it. A fist splits your lip, and you keep swinging, and somewhere in it the three of them decide you're more trouble than your purse is worth. They go, and you keep it.

failure.title: In the mud
failure.description: Your fists land, and your arms will be harder for it. But there are three of them, and one has a knife. You end up in the mud with your hand pressed to your side, and when you can look up, they're gone, with half your coin.

branches.title: Hold out your purse
branches.description: Hold out your purse, and let them take what they came for.

success.title: Now you know the way
