success.description: The thin one takes it, weighs it, and tips half of it into his own hand before he gives it back. "There," he says. "Now you know the way." They step aside to let you pass.

deserters.title: Deserters
deserters.intro: In the lee of the wall, past the last tents, four men sit round a fire too small to see from the road. Good boots, bad coats, and the coats turned inside out, so nobody can read the colours. One of them has a hand inside his coat before you've stopped walking.{if [q:origin] == 3} You know what a coat turned inside out means. You've thought about doing it yourself.{/if}

branches.title: Offer them bread
branches.description: Offer them bread. Men who can't go near the baker will pay for it.

success.title: You didn't see us
success.description: The one with his hand in his coat takes it out, with coin in it instead of a knife. He pays more than the baker would, and doesn't haggle. "You didn't see us," he says. It isn't a question.

branches.title: Ask to warm your hands at their fire
branches.description: Ask if you can warm your hands at their fire. Slowly, with your hands where they can see them.

success.title: The worst officer
success.description: They look at each other, and one of them shifts along the log. Nobody asks your name, and nobody gives his. You sit a bell with them, warming through, while they argue about which of their old officers was the worst. It's a long list.

failure.title: Walk on
failure.description: You keep your voice easy, and that comes easier every time. They don't believe a word of it. "Walk on," says the one with his hand in his coat, and he doesn't take it out until you have.

branches.title: Sit down at their fire
branches.description: Sit down at their fire as if you'd marched with them. In a way, you have.

success.title: A sergeant you both knew
success.description: "Which company?" one asks, and you tell him, and he names a sergeant you both knew. That's enough. They give you the warm end of the log and the last of something hot, and for a bell nobody out here is a stranger.

branches.title: Tell them the wardens would like to know where they sleep
branches.description: Tell them the wardens would like to know where they sleep. Then let them work out what your silence is worth.

success.title: A purse instead
success.description: They think about it for a long time. Then the one with his hand in his coat takes out a purse instead, and counts coin into your hand without a word. By dark their fire will be somewhere else, and you won't find it again.{if [q:trait] == 4} It doesn't trouble you. It never does.{/if}

failure.title: On their feet
failure.description: You say it well, and you'll say the next thing better. They don't let you say anything else. Four men who have already run from one army don't argue with a stranger: they get up, all at once.

dues-for-the-box.title: Dues for the Box
dues-for-the-box.intro: [who:regard-rope-mother] comes along the fires with the box under her arm and the book open on top of it. She stops in front of you and doesn't say anything. She doesn't have to.

branches.title: Put your dues in the box
branches.description: Put [c:club-dues] coin in the box.

success.title: A mark by your name
success.description: She watches the coin go in, and makes a mark beside your name with a stub of charcoal. "Good," she says, and goes on to the next fire.

branches.title: Tell her you haven't got it
branches.description: Tell her you haven't got it.

success.title: One line through the knot
success.description: She doesn't argue. She draws a line through your name in the book, and holds out her hand for the seal, and you give it to her. Then she takes your wrist, blackens the sail needle in the fire, and pricks one line through the knot. "What you paid stays in the box," she says. "It keeps the rest of us."

exploring-the-camp.title: Learning the Camp
exploring-the-camp.intro: {if [q:familiarity-camp] <= 1}You know the gate, the chapel and one fire. The rest of the camp is smoke, canvas and people who look past you, and it goes on further than it looked from the road.{else}{if [q:familiarity-camp] == 2}People at the fires you pass every day nod to you now. Past those fires, the camp still has corners you've only smelled.{else}You know the camp's paths without thinking about them. People tell you things they wouldn't tell a stranger, and some of it is even true.{/if}{/if}

branches.title: The river steps
branches.description: Find where the camp gets its water. Every camp has a place for it, and a rule about it.

success.title: Upstream of the yards
success.description:
Steps cut into the bank, worn hollow, and a queue of buckets. A girl with two of them tells you the rule without being asked. "Above the yards' ditch, for drinking. Below it, for washing. Below that, nothing."{if [q:origin] == 2}

Across the water, the rope gangs' old mooring rings are still in the bank, rusting. Mussels cling to the posts under them, where nobody from upriver thinks to look. You fill your pockets.{/if}

branches.title: The length of the camp
branches.description: Walk the camp road from the gate down to the dead-yards' fence, and see who lives where.

success.title: Every kind of fire
success.description: Families under carts. Soldiers with their coats spread out to dry. A man selling nails from a tray, one at a time. The tents get poorer as the road goes down and the smell of the yards gets stronger, until there's only the fence{if [q:trait] == 12}, and you stop well short of it{/if}.

success.title: A turnip in the rut
success.description:
Families under carts. Soldiers with their coats spread out to dry. The tents get poorer as the road goes down, and the smell of the yards gets stronger.

{if [q:trait] == 6}You see it from ten paces, in a cart rut by the crier's stand: a turnip, fallen off a cart and trodden in. You always see them.{else}In a cart rut by the crier's stand, something pale shows in the mud: a turnip, fallen off a cart and trodden in. Nobody is looking.{/if}

branches.title: Behind the haulers' fire
branches.description: Walk round the haulers' tents behind the fire, where their families live.

success.title: Drover and dead
success.description: Coils of tow-rope, grey with disuse, stacked like cheeses. Between them, children play drover and dead: one bangs a spoon on a pot, and the rest shuffle after with their arms stiff, until a mother shouts at them to stop.{if [q:trait] == 4} You walk straight through their game. They part for you, the way the dead part for a drover.{else}{if [q:origin] == 2} The knots on the coils are towing hitches. Your hands know them before your eyes do.{/if}{/if}

branches.title: The dead-yards' fence
branches.description: Go down along the dead-yards' fence by day, while the yards are half empty and the worn ones are being mended.

success.title: Through the slats
success.description: Most of the dead are out at work. The few left in the yard stand in a row, while a boy goes down it with a pot of pitch and a curved needle.{if [q:trait] == 12} You don't go close. You don't need to: you'd know that smell anywhere.{else}{if [q:binder] >= 1} Even from the fence you can see the seal on each brow, and the nail through it. You know what holds them.{else} Close to the slats, you can see a seal on each brow, with a nail through it: the same seals the living wear round their necks.{/if}{/if}

branches.title: Below the rapids
branches.description: Go down past the rapids, where the ferry folk wait for anyone who won't pay the bridge toll.

success.title: A hand with the boat
success.description: An old ferryman is dragging his boat up the shingle on his own, because nobody puts the dead on a ferry. You take the bow, and together you get it above the waterline. He has no coin to spare. He gives you a dried fish from the bottom of the boat instead.{if [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-wants] >= 1} A boat like this one, you think. Twelve coin, old.{/if}

failure.title: Wet to the knees
failure.description: Your arms are stronger for it, and your boots are full of river. The boat slides back down the shingle twice before the old ferryman waves you off. "Living work," he says. "Heavier than it looks."

branches.title: The hawkers' row
branches.description: Walk the hawkers' row under the wall, where the camp buys what the chapel won't give it.{if [q:origin] == 5} Every city has a row like this one.{/if}

success.title: Half price
success.description: Everything costs what an arrival will pay, and you aren't an arrival any more. You wait until the onion woman has sold to three of them at her first price, then offer her half for what's left. She calls you a thief, and takes it.

failure.title: The arrivals' price
failure.description: You learn the row's prices by paying them. The onion woman takes two coin for what she sells the camp for one, and looks at you as if you should thank her.

branches.title: The chapel door
branches.description: Read the papers nailed to the chapel door, where the camp goes to find out what the city wants of it.{if [q:origin] == 5} Every city has a door like this one.{/if}

success.title: Taken by the law
success.description: A notice of the church's terms, in a clerk's hand. The council's price for bread, crossed out and written again, higher. And a long list headed *Taken by the law*: the camp's dead that nobody came for. A name, where anyone knew one. Where nobody did, what they wore: a grey coat; a boy, about ten.

failure.title: A list of names
failure.description: Your eye for letters sharpens with every word you puzzle out. There aren't many you can. A price, crossed out and written higher. A long list under a heading you can't make out, some lines a name and some lines only a few words. The man beside you reads it over your shoulder, and spits.

branches.title: The washing stones
branches.description: Go down below the yards' ditch, where the camp does its washing, and kneel down with the others.

success.title: The camp's business
success.description: Your face is known here now, and the talk doesn't stop when you kneel down. Who's sick, and who's selling. Whose man went into the company's yard on his feet, and came out of it on his back. By the time your shirt is wrung out, you know more of the camp's business than you wanted to.{if [q:binder] >= 1} Nobody looks at your hands. In the river, everyone's hands are cold.{/if}

branches.title: The far fires
branches.description: Go out past the last tents, to the far fires, where the camp keeps its sick away from everyone else.

success.title: Fever, or hunger
success.description: Your hands know more than they did. A woman lets you look at her boy, because you look as if you know how. You know enough to say: keep him warm, give him water, keep the flies off him.{if [q:origin] == 3} You've seen camp fever go through a regiment.{/if}{if [q:trait] == 3} You stay longer than you meant to.{/if} She tells you which of the fires are fever, and which are only hunger.

failure.title: Too close
failure.description: You learn which fires are fever by getting too close to one. A man coughs on your hands, and a woman pulls her child out of your reach as if you were the sickness. You walk back fast, and scrub your hands in the river until they hurt.

branches.title: The mills on the rapids
branches.description: Go up the bank to where you can see the mills on the rapids, and the dead walking their wheels.

success.title: The wheels
success.description: Wheel after wheel along the rapids, and inside each one the dead walk, and walk, and the stones turn.{if [q:origin] == 1} At home it was oxen, and then it was the dead. You know the look of a walk that never stops.{/if}{if [q:trait] == 12} You watch from further back than anyone else on the bank.{/if}

success.title: Sweepings
success.description: Wheel after wheel along the rapids, and inside each one the dead walk, and the stones turn. A miller's cart tips at the top of the bank, and a sack splits. By the time the carter has finished swearing, half the camp has its hands in the flour, and so do you.

branches.title: The foot of the wall
branches.description: Walk the foot of the wall downstream, past the last of the tents, and look at it properly this time.

success.title: Downstream
success.description: Past the last tents the wall goes on alone, with the river at its foot. You walk it slowly, the way the man in the mud must have. Old stone, older at the bottom. Then the tanneries, and a smell that makes the dead-yards seem sweet, and below them the wall goes down into the river mud. Nobody comes here who doesn't have to. Somewhere along here, you think. You'll have to know the camp better to know where.

branches.title: Below the tanneries
branches.description: Go down into the mud below the tanneries, where the wall meets the river, and search along it.

success.title: The old drain
success.description: You go along the wall with one hand on the stone, ankle-deep, then knee-deep. Under a hanging mat of weed, the stone gives way to black: a hole in the wall the size of a barrel, with a lip of old brick. The air coming out of it smells of every year the city has stood. The old drain. You climb back up the bank with your legs cold to the bone, and the way in fixed in your head.

failure.title: Into it
failure.description: You're learning the river's moods, here as everywhere along it. Not well enough: the mud under the weed isn't mud. You go into the hole up to the chest, with the black water pulling at you and the wall's brick under your hands. The old drain. You get out on the second try, frozen and filthy, and you'll never forget where it is.

followed.title: Followed
followed.intro: A man has been behind you since the last fire. When you stop, he stops, and finds something to look at. When you go on, so does he. He's thin, his hands are empty, and he isn't in any hurry.{if [q:origin] == 3} You know that walk. In the camps, it came before a knife.{/if}

branches.title: Keep walking
branches.description: Keep walking as if you hadn't seen him, and lose him among the tents.

success.title: Lost among the tents
success.description: You don't look back. You turn between two tents, then two more, and come out on a path you don't know, further down than you meant to be. When you do look back, he's gone. Or he's somewhere you can't see.

branches.title: Keep walking, and lose him
branches.description: Keep walking, steady, and lose him among the last tents. Out here, nobody will step in if he catches you.

success.title: Nobody behind you
success.description: You keep your pace, and your nerve. A turn, a gap between two lean-tos, a ditch, and when you climb the far side there's nobody behind you. Only the camp, further out than ever, and very quiet.

failure.title: Between two tents
failure.description: Your nerve holds longer than it would have once. Not long enough. Between two tents he's suddenly in front of you, and when you turn, there's another one behind.

branches.title: Turn round and ask him what he wants
branches.description: Turn round and ask him, loud enough for the nearest tents to hear, what he wants.

success.title: Walking
success.description: "Nothing," he says. "Walking." But he's stopped, and the people at the nearest fire are looking at him now, not at you. You go on your way. When you look back, he's sitting at their fire as if he'd always been there.

failure.title: His friends
failure.description: Your voice comes out steadier than you feel, and next time it will come easier. He only grins. Two more come out from between the tents, and the nearest fire turns its back.

branches.title: Turn on him armed
branches.description: Turn on him with {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if} in your hand, and see how much he wants it.

success.title: Shown a stick
success.description: He looks at what's in your hand, then at your face, and decides. He walks off between the tents without hurrying, the way a dog goes when it's been shown a stick. You go on your way, and nobody follows.

failure.title: He was waiting for it
failure.description: Your hand is quicker than it was. His is quicker still: he was waiting for it. He's inside your reach before you can use it, and there's a knife, and then you're on the ground with your hand pressed to your side, and a second man is going through your coat. They take half your coin.

branches.title: Go back up toward the gate
branches.description: Turn back up the camp, toward the gate, where there are more people and more eyes.

success.title: Where people can see you
success.description: You walk back up the road, not fast, and don't look round until you're among the fires near the gate. He isn't there. He was never going to follow you that far. It's a bell gone, and nothing to show for it but the walk.

found-at-dawn.title: Found at Dawn

branches.title: Look at him
branches.description: Look at him.

success.title: Till noon
success.description: You look at him.

hands-for-the-dead.title: Hands for the Dead
hands-for-the-dead.intro:
Three hand-carts at the chapel door, not two, and {if [q:met-binder] == 0}the young woman in grey{else}[who:regard-binder]{/if} alone with them. She's washing an old woman's feet in a basin, and the water has gone grey. Behind her, the line for bread pretends not to look. She sees you watching.

"You've got two hands," she says. "Can you hold a head still while I wash it? Or fetch me water that isn't this?"

branches.title: Kneel down and hold the head
branches.description: Kneel down by her, and hold the old woman's head while she works.{if [q:origin] == 6} You know the words that go with this. You said them every morning, once.{/if}

success.title: The words for the dead
success.description: The head is heavier than you thought, and colder. While she washes, she says the words for the dead under her breath, and you find yourself saying them with her. She looks up at that. "Come back when you like," she says. "There's always more of them than there are of me. I can pay in bread."

failure.title: The wrong words
failure.description: The words for the dead stay with you after, the way she says them. You try to say them with her and get them wrong, and then the old woman's jaw drops open in your hands, and you nearly let go. She finishes for you without a word. Afterwards she dries her hands. "Everyone does that, the first time," she says. "Come back when you like. I can pay in bread."

branches.title: Fetch her clean water
branches.description: Take her basin down to the river steps, and bring back clean water.

success.title: Above the yards' ditch
success.description: Above the yards' ditch, for drinking. The water is so cold it makes your wrists ache. When you come back she's already on the next cart. She takes the basin without looking up. "Thank you," she says. "Come back when you like. There's always more of them than there are of me. I can pay in bread."

hands-for-the-yard.title: Hands for the Yard
hands-for-the-yard.intro:
A crowd outside the company tent, waiting to be picked for the yard. "Living hands!" the company man calls from the tent flap. "Two coin a shift, one for half!" He looks the crowd over like a farmer at a fair.{if [q:origin] == 2} The same company that put its dead on your towpath. It pays the same, too.{/if}

"Work well," he adds, "and the company looks after its own."

branches.title: Join the line
branches.description: Join the line, and wait to be looked over.

success.title: Your name in the company's list
success.description: The line moves a step at a time. When your turn comes, the company man squeezes your arm, turns your hands over, and writes your name on his list. "Come to the tent when you want a shift," he says. "One a day. We count the good ones."

branches.title: Catch the company man's eye
branches.description: Catch the company man's eye over the crowd, and tell him why it should be you.{if [q:origin] == 3} You've heard sergeants pick men out of a crowd. You know what they listen for.{/if}

success.title: That one
success.description: He points at you over the heads of the others. "That one." He writes your name on his list without asking how to spell it. "A shift a day, at the tent. We count the good ones." The man you stepped in front of says something you don't catch.

failure.title: That's the lot
failure.description: You find the words, and next time you'll find them faster. He looks straight past you and points at the man beside you instead. Then he counts heads, calls "That's the lot!" and lets the flap fall. The crowd breaks up. He'll be picking again another day.

he-heard-it-too.title: He Heard It Too
he-heard-it-too.intro:
{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] >= 3}[who:young-man] heard it lying down. He hasn't got up all day.{else}[who:young-man] heard it from the log by the fire. He didn't go to see the rider; he hasn't the legs for a crowd today.{/if} "Bread by the claim," he says. "Well. That settles it. I'll sign tomorrow. Company feeds its own." He tries to laugh, and the cough takes him, and goes on taking him, until [who:regard-rope-mother] holds a cup to his mouth.{if [q:prologue-young-man-cared] >= 2}

When he can talk again, he finds you with his eyes. "You've been good to me," he says. "Out here. Nobody's good out here."{/if}

branches.title: Sit up with him a while
branches.description: Sit down beside him, and stay a while.

success.title: The cathedral
success.description: He talks, when he has the breath. Not about the fleet. About the cathedral: he's seen it from the road every day since the summer, black against the sky, and he means to stand inside it once, when he has his brand, and look up. "They say it's so high inside that the incense never reaches the roof," he says. You sit with him until he sleeps.

branches.title: Put your coat over him for the night
branches.description: Put your coat over him for the night. You'll be colder. He's colder still.

success.title: Under your coat
success.description: He doesn't argue, which tells you more than anything. He pulls your coat up to his chin and shuts his eyes. You sit with your back to the fire and your arms wrapped round you, and listen to him breathe.

branches.title: Share your bread with him
branches.description: Break your bread, and give him the larger half.

success.title: Half a loaf
success.description: He eats it slowly, a crumb at a time, as if he's forgotten how. He gets most of it down. "Farm bread's better," he says, and grins, and for a moment he looks like he did the day you came.

branches.title: Leave him to sleep
branches.description: Leave him to sleep. Tomorrow he can sign, and they'll feed him.

success.title: Tomorrow
success.description: You leave him to it. His cough follows you round the fire, and then it settles, and you stop hearing it.

night-below-the-wall.title: Night Below the Wall
night-below-the-wall.intro:
Prime, and the sky is barely grey. {if [q:cold] >= 3}You slept, in the end, until the cold got into your bones.{else}{if [q:sleepiness] >= 3}You slept, in the end, in snatches.{else}You slept, in the end.{/if}{/if} The fire is out. The dead-yard's lanterns are still lit. Your hand has gone inside your clothes, to the one thing you would never sell, and found it before you were properly awake.

You're holding it now.

branches.title: Your parent's knife
branches.description: Your parent's knife, with the notches cut in the handle.{if [q:weapon-knife] > 0} Not the one on your belt: this one you never use.{/if}
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Fourteen notches
success.description: Fourteen notches. One for every risen it put down, back when families did their own. "Through the eye," they used to say, "and don't look at the face." Nobody needs a knife for that now. Now somebody drives a nail.

branches.title: The nail
branches.description: The nail, pulled, still black at the point.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Everything the family had
success.description: Four years your sister worked in the company's mill after she died. Then the family bought the nail back with everything it had, and a binder pulled it, and she lay down. It's the most expensive thing you've ever held. It weighs nothing.

branches.title: The cracked handbell
branches.description: A cracked handbell, its clapper wrapped in rag so it can't ring.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Twenty years
success.description: Your uncle carried it for twenty years, out of the yard at Prime and back at Vespers, driving other people's dead for hire. He never owned one of his own. It cracked the night he died, on the shelf, with nobody near it.

branches.title: A seal that isn't yours
branches.description: A pewter seal on a cord. Not yours: the stamp is a barge, a handbell, a hand.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Your mother's
success.description: Your mother's. She wore it until the stamp was smooth, and the company stamped her a new one; she kept this one. The new one is nailed to her brow now, in their yards somewhere, if she hasn't worn out. You've looked for her face in every column you've passed.

branches.title: Your grandfather's share
branches.description: A printed share in a ship across the sea, gone soft as cloth from folding.{if [q:prologue-bought-a-share] > 0} Older than the one you bought yesterday, and from the same ship.{/if}
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: One day
success.description: Your grandfather bought it forty years ago and never sailed: the ship was always still filling. He kept it in his hat. "One day," he used to say. Then he died, and was bound, and you kept the share.

branches.title: The printed page
branches.description: A page from the anatomist's book, a cheap print, folded in eight.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Every part lettered
success.description: A man's head, opened like a book, every part lettered. Somebody printed ten thousand of these the year after the siege, and sold them at fairs for a penny. You can't read all of it. Nobody can. Everybody has tried.

branches.title: The pouch of ashes
branches.description: A leather pouch of ashes, tied tight.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: Nobody's
success.description: Your own dead, burned your own way, in a ditch, with nobody's permission. No company works them. No church does either. It was a crime. It was the cheapest thing you ever did, and the only one you're sure of.

branches.title: The lock of hair
branches.description: A lock of hair, tied with thread.
branches.hoverText: A keepsake. It goes in your kit, and starts its own story later.

success.title: What a minute buys
success.description: You cut it while the company's men waited at the door with the cart, polite, the way they always are. They had a claim. You had a knife and a minute. This is what the minute bought.

no-way-past.title: No Way Past
no-way-past.intro: The man with the cudgel is close enough to touch, and the boy has another stone ready. "Last time of asking," the woman says. "Coin."

branches.title: Fight them armed
branches.description: Get {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your own cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if} up between you and the cudgel, and make them pay for every coin.

success.title: The day's takings
success.description: The next blow lands on what's in your hand, not on you, and the one after that on your shoulder. Then it's you swinging, and they're the ones backing off. They run, and the woman drops a purse as she goes: the day's takings, off somebody else.

failure.title: Until the cold gets you up
failure.description: Your arm learns where the cudgel comes from, for next time. This time it comes from the other side. The cudgel takes your legs, and the boy's stones take the rest. They go through your coat and take half your coin, and you lie in the mud by the last tents, watching the smoke go over, until the cold gets you up.

branches.title: Fight them with your fists
branches.description: Get inside the cudgel's swing, where it can't hurt you, and use your fists.

success.title: Inside the swing
success.description: You get in close, where a cudgel is only a stick, and he isn't brave any more. A stone glances off your head, and then the three of them are running, and the woman drops a purse as she goes: somebody else's, from earlier.

failure.title: The boy's stones
failure.description: Each fight hardens your arms. This one isn't enough: the cudgel catches you coming in, and the boy's stones do the rest. They take half your coin, and leave you in the mud by the last tents until the cold gets you up.

branches.title: Hand it over
branches.description: Hand over your purse. There's nothing else for it now.

success.title: You should have done that first
success.description: She counts it with her thumb, and gives you half of it back. "You should have done that first," she says, and they let you go.

nobodys-now.title: Nobody's Now
nobodys-now.intro: Out here, things lie where they fall, and stay there until someone picks them up. Today, that someone could be you.

branches.title: The river bank
branches.description: Something dark lies at the waterline below the last fires.

success.title: The river had them first
success.description: A pair of boots, still laced, left on the stones where the river dropped them. Good leather, a little shrunk. Nobody comes to claim them, and nobody will. You pour the water out, and take them.

branches.title: The washing stones
branches.description: The women at the washing stones have gone. Something glints between two of the stones.

success.title: A saint in the mud
success.description: A pilgrim's badge, stamped in lead, with its pin bent. A saint nobody here could name. Somebody walked a long way to earn it. You straighten the pin, and wipe the mud off on your sleeve.

not-at-the-fire.title: Not at the Fire
not-at-the-fire.intro: [who:regard-rope-mother] catches up with you on the camp road, out of breath, with the box under her arm. "Wasn't at the fire," she says. "Looked for you at first light." She looks up the hill, toward the chapel, and back at you. Then she opens the book on the lid. "Your dues. Yesterday's."

branches.title: Pay her what you owe
branches.description: Pay her the [c:club-dues] coin, here on the road.

success.title: Found you
success.description: She makes her mark beside your name, a day late, with the book balanced on her knee. "Sleep where you like," she says. "Pay where I can find you." She goes back down the road at her own pace.

branches.title: Hold out your wrist
branches.description: Tell her you haven't got it, and hold out your wrist.

success.title: On the road
success.description: She draws a line through your name, there in the road, and holds out her hand for the seal. Then she holds the sail needle in her pipe bowl till it's black, and pricks one line through the knot on your wrist. People step round the two of you and don't look. "What you paid stays in the box," she says, and goes back down to her fire.

not-that-simple.title: More Than It Sees
not-that-simple.intro: The queue sees a body under the dust, and decides what you are. It has been deciding all the way from home.

branches.title: A man, in a woman's body
branches.description: A woman's body, as the world sees it. A man, as you know it.

success.title: A man
success.description: The carter behind you calls you "mistress". He's wrong, and he'll never know it. You stopped correcting carters a long time ago.

branches.title: Neither, in a woman's body
branches.description: A woman's body. Neither a woman nor a man.

success.title: In between
success.description: The carter behind you calls you "mistress". It doesn't fit. It will do, for a carter, on a road, for a mile.

branches.title: A woman, in a man's body
branches.description: A man's body, as the world sees it. A woman, as you know it.

success.title: A woman
success.description: The recruiter's boy with the drum looks you over the way a dealer looks over a horse. He sees a man. You let him see what he likes, and keep the rest.

branches.title: Neither, in a man's body
branches.description: A man's body. Neither a man nor a woman.

success.title: In between
success.description: The recruiter's boy calls you "friend" and means "soldier". Neither word is yours. You have answered to both on the road, and kept your own name underneath.

nothing-to-lose.title: Nothing to Lose
nothing-to-lose.intro: Three of them, between you and the way back: a man with a cudgel, a boy with a stone, and a woman who does the talking. "Coin," she says. "Whatever's in the coat."{if [q:appearance] >= 3} "Nice coat," says the boy.{/if} None of them has eaten today. None of them cares much what happens next.

branches.title: Hand it over
branches.description: Hand over your purse. It's only coin, and there are three of them.

success.title: Less to lose
success.description: You hold out the purse. The woman takes it, counts it with her thumb, and gives you half of it back, which is somehow worse. "Now you've less to lose," she says, and they step aside to let you by.

branches.title: Go for the one with the cudgel
branches.description: Go for the man with the cudgel first, with {if [q:weapon-knife] > 0}your knife{/if}{if [q:weapon-cudgel] > 0}your own cudgel{/if}{if [q:weapon-boat-hook] > 0}your boat-hook{/if}{if [q:weapon-hanger] > 0}your sword{/if}, and hope the other two run.

success.title: Somebody else's purse
success.description: The cudgel catches your shoulder on the way in, and then you're inside his reach and he isn't brave any more. He runs, and the boy runs with him, and the woman drops a purse as she goes: what they took off somebody else today. There's more in it than you'd think, this far out.

failure.title: In the mud by the last tents
failure.description: Your arm learns the weight of a real fight, and it will be quicker next time. Not now. The cudgel takes your legs, and the boy's stone takes the rest. They go through your coat and take half your coin, and when they've gone you lie in the mud by the last tents until the cold gets you up.

branches.title: Talk to the woman
branches.description: Talk to the woman. She's the one who decides, and she's hungry, not stupid.

success.title: Next time, bring bread
success.description: You talk, and she listens, and it takes a long time. Somewhere in it she decides you're more trouble than you're worth. "Go on, then," she says. "Next time, bring bread." They let you by with everything you came with.

failure.title: She hears you out
failure.description: The words come easier every time you need them. Not easily enough: she hears you out, then nods to the man with the cudgel, and he steps in close.

branches.title: Run for it
branches.description: Turn and run, back up the camp, before they close the gap.{if [q:feature-limp] > 0} With your leg, it's a gamble.{/if}

success.title: Back up the camp
success.description: You run. Your legs carry you up past the last tents, past the lean-tos, and you don't stop until the yards' fence is beside you and you can hear people at the fires. Nobody followed you. The smell of the yards has never been so welcome.

failure.title: The boy is faster
failure.description: Your legs are stronger for every step. Not strong enough: the boy is faster, and his stone takes you behind the knee. You go down in the mud, and they're over you before you can get up.

on-your-back.title: On Your Back
on-your-back.intro:
A scream, two tents over, and your hand moves before you know it has. It's only a drover, cursing one of his dead, who has sat down in the mud and won't get up. The camp goes back to its business. Nobody below the wall sleeps unarmed, with the dead lands a day to the east.

What did your hand find?

branches.title: A knife
branches.description: A knife. Long enough for a throat, short enough for a sleeve.
branches.hoverText: Arms +1, worn in the melee slot.

success.title: A knife
success.description: It has done for a risen once, through the eye. You cleaned it twice afterwards, and it still didn't feel clean.

branches.title: A cudgel
branches.description: A cudgel: oak, with iron round the head.
branches.hoverText: Arms +1, worn in the melee slot.

success.title: A cudgel
success.description: Heavy, honest, and it does for a skull. The wardens at the arch won't count a stick as a weapon. You do.

branches.title: A boat-hook
branches.description: A boat-hook: a hauler's pole with an iron hook.
branches.hoverText: Arms +1, worn in the melee slot.

success.title: A boat-hook
success.description: Eight feet of ash and a hook. It keeps a risen at arm's length, and then some. Haulers swear by it.

branches.title: A wheel-lock pistol
branches.description: A wheel-lock pistol in your belt. Unloaded.
branches.hoverText: Shot +1, worn in the ranged slot. Unloaded.

success.title: A pistol
success.description: You have the key to wind it, and no powder. Powder costs more than bread this year. Still: people see the butt in your belt and give you room.

branches.title: A soldier's short sword
branches.description: A soldier's short sword, heavy and plain, carried home from the wars.
branches.hoverText: Arms +2, worn in the melee slot. Only a soldier would have one.

success.title: A short sword
success.description: Made for close work in a press of bodies, living and not. There's a nick in the edge from a dead man's neck-bone. You keep meaning to grind it out.

one-of-ours.title: One of Ours
one-of-ours.intro:
In the blanket is the old man who passed you the salt {if [time:day] >= 2}yesterday{else}at noon{/if}, his face as brown and creased as an old glove. He died mucking out the yard, they say, between one shovel and the next.

Nobody goes for the company man, or the chapel. An old man with rags wound round his hands is already at the fire: the club's binder. He holds his hands out to [who:regard-rope-mother], and she unlocks the box.

"[c:release-price]," he says. "Same as anyone."

"Two hundred, for the club. Always has been."

"It's a colder winter. My hands are colder." He waits. She counts it out on the lid in stacks of ten, two hundred and forty, and tips the box to the firelight so he can see how little is left.

branches.title: Take a corner of the blanket
branches.description: Take a corner of the blanket, and help them lay him by the fire.

success.title: Heavier than he looks
success.description:
He's heavier than he looks, all of him gone stiff. You lay him by the fire, and the binder kneels. He lays the dead man's own seal on his brow, says the words, and drives the nail through it. The dead man's eyes open, and his hand twitches toward the binder's wrist. In the same breath the binder draws out the nail and the seal, and the hand drops, and the old man is still for good.

[who:regard-rope-mother] opens a book on her knee and makes a small mark beside one name. She looks at you over it. "You carried him," she says. "That counts."

branches.title: Stand back and watch
branches.description: Stand back, and watch.

success.title: Still
success.description:
The binder kneels. He lays the dead man's own seal on his brow, says the words, and drives the nail through it, and the dead man's eyes open. Everyone round the fire leans away at once. Then the binder draws out the nail and the seal, in the same breath, and the old man lies down for good, as if he'd only wanted to look at them one more time.

[who:regard-rope-mother] runs her finger down a page of her book to his name. "Forty years he paid into that box," she says, to nobody. "Forty years, for this."

branches.title: Ask the man beside you what's happening
branches.description: Ask the man beside you, low, what they're doing.

success.title: Not a day
success.description:
"Letting him go," he says, without taking his eyes off the body. "Dead men get up, you know that. So the club's binder binds him first, and a bound man does as he's told, and doesn't go for us. Then he lets him go again, so the company can't have him." The dead man's eyes open, and close. "There. Not a day's work for anyone, after his last."

He lets his breath out. "Paid up to last week, he was. Good thing."

out-of-the-river.title: Out of the River
out-of-the-river.intro:
A man comes up the river bank below the wall, where there are no steps, wet to the chest and black with mud to the eyes. He has a sack on his shoulder. He sees you see him. Then he's off between the tents, and the sack with him.

Nobody comes up out of the river there. Not unless they've come from somewhere.

branches.title: Go after him, quietly
branches.description: Go after him, quietly, and see where he takes the sack.

success.title: City bread
success.description: You keep two tents behind him all the way to the hawkers' row. He opens the sack there: loaves, still warm, with a city baker's stamp on the crust. Bread from inside the walls, and he came up out of the river with it. You don't let him see you. You don't need to ask. There's a way under the wall, and he knows it.

failure.title: Mind your own
failure.description: You're quieter than you were, and you'll be quieter still. Not quiet enough: he turns at the end of a row and is waiting for you. "Mind your own," he says, low, with his hand inside his coat. You let him go, and he's gone into the tents. But the mud on him came from somewhere.

branches.title: Go down to where he came up
branches.description: Go down the bank to where he came up, and see what's there.

success.title: Mud and stone
success.description: Nothing but mud, and his footprints going up out of the water, and the wall. Whatever way he came, the river has covered it. You stand there until your feet are cold through. The foot of the wall runs on downstream, toward the tanneries. Somewhere along it, there's a way.

shivering.title: Shivering
shivering.intro:
Your teeth won't stop. The wind comes off the river and goes straight through what you're wearing, and you can't feel your fingers. There's a coat rolled up and tied to your belt.

[You can put your coat on and take it off in the Kit tab, whenever no card is open. Each piece of clothing shows its Warmth there. While what you wear is not warm enough for the weather, Cold rises; when it is, Cold falls.]

branches.title: Not now
branches.description: Not now. Keep moving, and keep the coat for later.

success.title: Teeth chattering
success.description: You stamp your feet and blow on your hands. It doesn't help much.

branches.title: Put on your coat
branches.description: Untie the coat from your belt and put it on.

success.title: Warmer
success.description: It smells of the road and it's creased in a dozen places, but the wind stops getting in. Bit by bit, the shaking stops.

struck-through.title: Struck Through
struck-through.intro: {if [q:club-dues-owed] >= 3}[who:regard-rope-mother] finds you at first light, with the book open on top of the box. She's been looking for you. "Two days," she says. "Your dues."{else}[who:regard-rope-mother] finds you at first light, with the book open on top of the box. "Yesterday," she says. "Your dues."{/if}

branches.title: Find the coin
branches.description: Find the [c:club-dues] coin, and put it in the box.

success.title: Late
success.description: She makes her mark beside your name, a day late. "Once," she says, and goes back to her fire.

branches.title: Hold out your wrist
branches.description: Hold out your wrist.

success.title: Struck through
success.description: She draws a line through your name, and holds out her hand for the seal. Then she blackens the sail needle and pricks one line through the knot on your wrist, neat as a splice. "What you paid stays in the box," she says. "It keeps the rest of us." She goes back to her fire, and doesn't look back.

talk-binder.title: At the Binder's Table
talk-binder.intro: {if [q:prologue-binder-told-age] + [q:prologue-binder-told-claim] + [q:prologue-binder-told-paupers] + [q:prologue-binder-told-young-man] + [q:prologue-binder-told-grey] == 0}[who:regard-binder] sets her stamp aside and holds her hands over the fire pan while she listens.{else}{if [q:prologue-binder-told-age] + [q:prologue-binder-told-claim] + [q:prologue-binder-told-paupers] + [q:prologue-binder-told-young-man] + [q:prologue-binder-told-grey] == 1}She waits, hands over the coals, and the line behind you shifts its feet.{else}{if [q:prologue-binder-told-age] + [q:prologue-binder-told-claim] + [q:prologue-binder-told-paupers] + [q:prologue-binder-told-young-man] + [q:prologue-binder-told-grey] == 2}She flexes her fingers over the fire pan. "Well?"{else}She glances at the line, and back at you, and her hands don't leave the coals.{/if}{/if}{/if}

branches.title: How old she is
branches.description: Ask her how old she is.

success.title: Twenty-six
success.description: "Twenty-six," she says, and tucks a grey lock back under her hood with fingers that are blue to the knuckle.

branches.title: Tell her the grey suits her
branches.description: Tell her the grey suits her.

success.title: Somewhere warmer
success.description: She looks at you over the fire pan for longer than the line would like. "Liar," she says. "It suits nobody." She doesn't tuck the lock back under her hood, though. "Say that again somewhere warmer, and I might believe you."

branches.title: What a church claim means
branches.description: Ask her what a church claim means, when it comes to it.

success.title: A term
success.description:
"When you die, I bind you, or whoever has this table then. You work a term in the church's yards, and then you're released."

"Doctrine says a year for small sins and longer for big ones," she says, her hands back over the coals. "The cathedral sets the terms by how many hands its yards need that year, so a saint and a cutpurse can work the same three years."

branches.title: The paupers
branches.description: Ask her why she releases paupers and takes nothing for it.

success.title: Hers to waste
success.description:
"Not for nothing," she says, and turns her blue hands over above the coals. "If I bind someone and unbind them the same hour, the church gets no term out of them, and I pay the whole cost myself. The cathedral calls it waste."

She almost smiles. "It's mine to waste."

branches.title: About the young man
branches.description: Talk about [who:young-man].

success.title: What she heard
success.description: {if [q:prologue-binder-released-the-young-man] > 0}"Don't thank me," she says, and blows on her blue fingers. "You carried him up from the fire. I paid the rest. That's how it goes at this table." She turns her hands over above the coals. "He had a good face. I'll remember it a while. Not for ever. Nothing's for ever, with this."{/if}{if [q:prologue-sold-the-young-man] > 0}"The company's binder did him by noon," she says. "He'll be on a mill wheel by now." She doesn't say anything else, and she doesn't need to.{/if}{if [q:prologue-burned-the-young-man] > 0}"I saw the smoke." She is quiet a while. "The cathedral will say you stole him from the company, and damned him besides." She looks at you. "I don't say that."{/if}{if [q:prologue-bound-the-young-man] > 0}She looks at your hands, then at your face. "You'll want to be careful," she says, very low. "There's a warden on that gate who feels for the cold, and I'm not the only one who can see it on you."{/if}{if [q:prologue-left-the-young-man] > 0}"The ditch," she says. "I'd have done him for nothing, if anyone had asked." She goes back to her stamp. Nobody asked.{/if}

branches.title: Let her get back to work
branches.description: Let her get back to her stamp.

success.title: The next in line
success.description: She nods. Someone is already waiting on the bench behind you, with a coin for a seal.

talk-rope-mother.title: By the Fire
talk-rope-mother.intro: {if [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club-cost] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-saving] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-why-here] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-wants] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-young-man] == 0}[who:regard-rope-mother] knocks her pipe out on a coil of old rope and waits. She talks the way she used to haul: in short pulls, with a rest between.{else}{if [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club-cost] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-saving] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-why-here] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-wants] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-young-man] == 1}She packs the pipe again, slowly, and waits.{else}{if [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club-cost] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-saving] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-why-here] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-wants] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-young-man] == 2}She lights the pipe from a twig and looks at you through the smoke.{else}She watches the road, and you, in about equal measure.{/if}{/if}{/if}

branches.title: The box at her feet
branches.description: {if [q:prologue-saw-the-release] > 0}Ask her about the club that let the old man go.{else}Ask her about the box under her feet.{/if}

success.title: The box
success.description: "Burial club." She taps the box with her heel. "Started with my rope gang. Now it's anyone I'll speak for: washerwomen, porters, a tanner or two." She opens the book on her knee, all names and little marks. "[c:club-dues] coin in the box every [c:club-dues-every] days. One of us goes, I pay the binder out of it, the same hour, and sit with them till he comes. Miss your dues, you're out, and what you paid stays in." She shuts the book. "[c:club-fee] coin to get your name in. And I have to say you're good for it."

branches.title: Why the club costs coin
branches.description: Ask her why anyone pays to have their death held, when the company pays you to sign yours.

success.title: Buying it back
success.description: "The company buys your death." She knocks her pipe out on the box. "Two coin, and it's theirs, and all the work that's left in you." She packs the pipe again, slowly. "We buy ours back. All of us together, a little at a time, so nobody has to find the whole price alone when it comes."

branches.title: Why not save for it
branches.description: Ask her why nobody just puts by the price of a binder for themselves.

success.title: Nobody lives that long
success.description: "A binder wants [c:release-price] coin to let you go on your own. Years off his life, every one he does, and he charges for them." She shrugs. "Put by a coin a day, if you work every day, and you don't eat much, and nobody knocks you on the head for it. Nobody out here lives that long." She rests her heel on the box. "So we do it together."

branches.title: Why she's still out here
branches.description: Ask her why she's still out here, with a seal round her neck and the gate just up the road.

success.title: All these hands know
success.description: "Seal gets me in, any morning I like." She taps the knot at her neck. "And do what? Forty years on a rope. That's all these hands know." She turns them over in the firelight, scarred across both palms. "In there they've got the dead for hauling. Out here somebody has to keep the box."

branches.title: What she wants
branches.description: Ask her what she wants, if it isn't the city.

success.title: A boat
success.description:
She doesn't have to think about it. "A boat. A little one. Ferry folk across below the rapids, where the bridge toll's too dear." She taps her pipe on her knee. "Nobody puts the dead on a ferry. Folk won't sit next to them. That's living work, that is."

"Twelve coin, for an old one." A pause. "I've got four."

branches.title: About the young man
branches.description: Talk about [who:young-man].

success.title: What she thinks
success.description: {if [q:prologue-sold-the-young-man] > 0}"You did what the camp does," she says. "Somebody was going to. Don't expect me to like you for it." She doesn't look at you. "He wanted to see the cathedral. Told me so."{/if}{if [q:prologue-binder-released-the-young-man] > 0}"That was well done," she says. "For a boy you'd known a few days." She nods slowly. "It cost you a walk up to the gate. It cost her more. Did you see her hands, after?"{/if}{if [q:prologue-burned-the-young-man] > 0}"Nobody's," she says. "Nobody's, for ever." She smiles at the road. "The wardens will be at us for a month. Worth it."{/if}{if [q:prologue-bound-the-young-man] > 0}{if [q:prologue-released-the-young-man] > 0}"You let him go," she says. "Cold hands, and you let him go anyway." She nods, once. "That's more than most binders do for nothing."{else}"Cold hands," she says. "I should've known from the way you held the bowl." She looks toward [who:young-man], wherever you've left him. "Let him go, when you can. Before he wears out on you."{/if}{/if}{if [q:prologue-left-the-young-man] > 0}"The law," she says. "Spade and a ditch." She smokes. "He was going to sign, you know. Today. Two coin and a hot dinner."{/if}

branches.title: Leave her to her pipe
branches.description: Leave her to her pipe and the road.

success.title: Back to the road
success.description: She nods, and goes back to watching the road.

talk-young-man.title: On the Log
talk-young-man.intro: {if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] <= 1}[who:young-man] shifts along the log to make room, and coughs, and grins as if the cough is a joke he's in on.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] == 2}[who:young-man] is sitting as close to the fire as he can get without burning, sweating and shivering at once. He makes room for you all the same.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] >= 3}[who:young-man] is lying by the fire under a blanket. He turns his head when you sit down, and that's all he turns.{/if}

branches.title: Where he's from
branches.description: Ask him where he's from.

success.title: The farms
success.description: "Downriver. The farms past the second bridge." He pokes the fire. "The family's claim was sold on to a company, the land and everyone on it, living and dead. My mother's ploughing our own field now, for them, with a nail in her head." He says it lightly, the way you'd tell someone the weather. "So I came up here. Sign on, get in, get a brand. Somewhere with a roof."

branches.title: The cough
branches.description: Ask him about the cough.

success.title: The damp
success.description: {if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] <= 1}"The damp," he says. "Gets in your chest out here. Everyone's got it." He's been below the wall since the summer, sleeping on the ground, eating what the pot has. "It'll go when I'm inside. There's a surgeon by the road, under an awning, but he wants a seal before he'll look at you. Wants to know who'll come for you, if you die on his table."{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] == 2}"It's nothing," he says, and his teeth chatter on it. He's been below the wall since the summer, on the ground, on what the pot has. "The surgeon by the road won't look at a fever without a seal. Wants to know who'll come for you, if you die on his table." He laughs, and wishes he hadn't. "Fair enough. Nobody would."{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] >= 3}It takes him a long time to answer. "Since the summer," he says. "The ground. The damp. Nothing in the pot." He shuts his eyes. "The surgeon by the road wants a seal. I asked." A long breath. "I'll be all right when I'm inside."{/if}

branches.title: Signing on with the company
branches.description: Ask him whether he means to sign on with the company.

success.title: Two who stand together
success.description: {if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] <= 2}"When they'll pass me." He nods at the company tent. "Four good shifts in the yard, and they sign you. I've done two, and fallen down in one." He looks at you sideways. "They take two who stand together, in the line. Work beside me one morning? You carry the heavy end when I cough, I make you laugh."{else}"When I can stand," he says. "Four good shifts, and they sign you. I've done two." He looks at the company tent, a long way off across the fire. "You'll sign before me, at this rate. Don't let them put the brand on crooked."{/if}

branches.title: Let him rest
branches.description: Let him rest.

success.title: Back to the fire
success.description: "Come back," he says. "I'm not going anywhere."

the-bakers-cart.title: The Baker's Cart
the-bakers-cart.intro: The baker's cart at the edge of the camp, and the crowd held back from it by his boy with a stick. Warm bread, and a price chalked on a board{if [q:crisis-bread-dear] > 0}, chalked over since the fleet was late{/if}. "Price of bread's the price of bread," the baker says, to anyone who looks at it too long.

branches.title: Buy two loaves
branches.description: {if [q:crisis-bread-dear] > 0}Pay [c:bread-price] coin for two loaves: four times what bread should cost.{else}Pay [c:bread-price] coin for two loaves: three times what bread should cost.{/if}

success.title: Two loaves
success.description: The baker bites one of your coins, and drops the rest in his apron without counting them. Two dark loaves, still warm. You carry them back through the crowd with your arms round them.

the-camp-afterwards.title: The Camp Afterwards

branches.title: Go on
branches.description: Go on. {if [q:claim] > 0}{if [q:mark-fresh] > 0}You have your claim, and a mark that needs its three nights to heal before the wardens can read it.{else}You have your claim, and the gate is open.{/if}{else}You still need a way in.{/if}

success.title: A way in
success.description: You get up.

the-camp-road.title: The Camp Road
the-camp-road.intro: {if [q:depth-camp] == 0}The camp road runs down from the gate, past the haulers' fire and the fires you know, toward the dead-yards. Below them the smoke is thinner, and so are the people.{/if}{if [q:depth-camp] == 1}The road goes on down, rutted and wet. Nobody here nods to you. Below the yards' fence, the wind carries the smell of the yards straight into the tents.{/if}{if [q:depth-camp] == 2}Downwind of the yards, the tents give out into lean-tos and holes in the bank. Further down, past the last of them, a few fires smoke where the camp gives up.{/if}{if [q:depth-camp] == 3}The far camp. People here look at what you carry before they look at your face. Past the last tents, the bank runs on toward the tanneries, and a few fires burn that nobody admits to.{/if}{if [q:depth-camp] >= 4}The last fires. Past them there's only the wall, the river mud and the stink of the tanneries. The gate is a long walk back up the road.{/if}

branches.title: Past the fires you know
branches.description: Go on down the road, past the fires that know your face, and see who lives below them.

success.title: Strangers' fires
success.description: Past the haulers' fire, the faces stop knowing you. A woman takes her washing in as you pass{if [q:appearance] >= 3}, with a long look at your coat{/if}. Children follow you for a while, then lose interest. The road goes on down, and so do you.

branches.title: On below the yards
branches.description: Follow the road on past the yards' fence, where the wind carries the smell into the tents.

success.title: Downwind
success.description: The yards' fence runs beside the road, and the smell comes with it: lime and old meat. The tents down here are patched with sacking. A man sitting in a doorway watches you go by, and doesn't look away when you look at him.

branches.title: Down to the last tents
branches.description: Go on down to the last tents, where the camp's poorest live.

success.title: What people throw away
success.description: The tents give out. Lean-tos; a cart with no wheels and a family under it; holes dug into the bank, with a sack for a door. Everything here is something somebody threw away. Talk stops when you come near, and starts again behind you.{if [q:origin] == 4} You've seen camps like this one, on the road out of the dead lands. They don't get better.{/if}

branches.title: Out past the last tents
branches.description: Go out past the last tents, to the fires nobody admits to.

success.title: Fires nobody admits to
success.description: Past the last tents the bank is bare, and the wall goes on alone toward the tanneries. A few fires burn in the lee of it, small and low, the kind people light when they don't want to be found. Someone kicks earth over one as you come.

branches.title: Back up the road
branches.description: Walk back up the road, toward the gate and the fires you know. It's uphill all the way.

success.title: Uphill all the way
success.description: You walk back up the road, against the slope and the wind. The tents get better, and the fires get bigger, until the faces around them are faces you've seen before{if [q:familiarity-camp] >= 2}, and one or two of them nod{/if}. It's a bell later than you thought.

the-chapel-at-the-gate.title: The Chapel at the Gate

branches.title: The chapel's bread
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 5}There's a line for the chapel's bread. You won't stand in it. Not here, not for them.{else}Join the line for the chapel's bread.{/if}

success.title: Black bread
success.description: Two bells in the wind, a step at a time, behind a man who counts the people ahead of him out loud. At the door, black bread and a blessing. The blessing is free. The bread is stamped with the chapel's mark, like everything here.

success.title: Gone before your turn
success.description: Since the news, the line goes down past the hand-carts. Two bells in the wind, a step at a time, and then the word comes back along it before you reach the door: no more bread today. [who:regard-binder] comes out to bless what's left of the line, and sends it away.

branches.title: Talk to the binder
branches.description: Sit on the bench by the young woman's table, and talk to her.

success.title: A word with the binder
success.description: You sit on the bench. She finishes the seal she's stamping, and looks up. "[who:regard-binder]," she says. "Don't sit long. There's a line."

branches.title: Talk to the binder
branches.description: Sit on the bench by her table, and talk to her.

success.title: A word with the binder
success.description: You sit down. She finishes the seal she's stamping first.

branches.title: Help with the camp's dead
branches.description: Help [who:regard-binder] with the camp's dead: wash them, lay them straight, and say the words while she works.

success.title: Bread, and cold hands
success.description: An old man, a girl of ten, a soldier with no boots. You wash each one in water that makes your hands ache, and lay them straight, and say the words for the dead with her, and then she binds and unbinds them, one after another, and holds her hands over the fire pan between. At the end she gives you a loaf with the chapel's mark on it. "Same again tomorrow," she says. "There'll be more."

failure.title: She finishes for you
failure.description: The words for the dead come a little easier each time you say them. Not easily enough: a boy's mother is kneeling by the cart, and you stumble over his name, and she starts to wail. [who:regard-binder] takes over without a word, and you're left holding the basin. At the end she gives you a loaf anyway. "It's hard the first few times," she says. "And after."

branches.title: Buy a church claim
branches.description: Buy a church claim. [c:church-claim-price] coin, and when you die, your body works a term for its sins before it's released.
branches.hoverText: The church will hold your death. When you die, you will be bound and work a term in the church's yards as penance. Then the church unbinds you. Its mark is pricked into the back of your hand, and the gate won't read it for three nights.

success.title: A chapel and a nail
success.description:
She takes your name and your coin, and presses the stamp into soft pewter: a little chapel, and a nail. She ties the cord round your neck with cold fingers. Then she turns your right hand over on the table, and pricks the same chapel and nail into the back of it with a needle and lamp-black, slowly, while the line waits.

"A term," she says, "then release. I'll do it myself, if I'm still at this table. [who:regard-binder]," she adds. "If you need me."

branches.title: Sleep in her home
branches.description: Go round behind [who:regard-binder]'s table, lift the latch, and unroll the straw mattress by her stove.

success.title: A door that shuts
success.description: Her stove ticks as it cools. The river comes through the wall, and the gate's bar, and the yards' handbells, a long way off. In here there's a door that shuts. You sleep without keeping one ear open.

branches.title: Too cold to sleep
branches.description: You brought the cold in with you, and lying still on her floor, it stays in your bones. Sit up close to her stove until it lets go.

success.title: Knees to the stove
success.description: You sit with your knees to the stove door, close enough to scorch your cuffs, while it burns down. Somewhere past midnight the cold lets go. You sleep where you sit, and wake stiff, with your back against the cooling iron.

branches.title: Buy charcoal for her stove
branches.description: A boy goes round the chapel at night with a sack of charcoal, a coin a bucket. Enough to keep her stove in till morning.

success.title: Banked up
success.description: The boy bites your coin and tips the bucket into her box. You bank the stove up high. In her sleep [who:regard-binder] turns over towards the warmth, and the cold stays on the far side of the door. You sleep deep, and dream of nothing at all.

branches.title: Too shaken to sleep
branches.description: Every time you shut your eyes, it's there again. [who:regard-binder] is still up, stamping tomorrow's seals by the stove. Sit up with her till it passes.

success.title: Tomorrow's seals
success.description: She doesn't ask what's wrong. She talks while she stamps: the girl who brings the pewter, the cathedral's clerk who counts it, the goat that got into the chapel one winter and ate a prayer book. Somewhere between the goat and the clerk, your hands stop shaking. You fall asleep sitting up against her wall, and wake with her blanket over you.

branches.title: Share her mourners' brandy
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 10}She keeps a bottle under her table for mourners who go white at the hand-carts. She holds it up. You shake your head. You always do.{else}She keeps a bottle under her table for mourners who go white at the hand-carts. Put a loaf on her shelf for the morning, and drink until you stop seeing it.{/if}

success.title: The bottom of the bottle
success.description: She pours, and doesn't pour one for herself. The brandy is rough, and burns all the way down, and then the room goes soft at the edges: the stove, the seals, her blue hands round the bottle. The next thing you know it's grey morning, and your head pounds in time with the stove's ticking.

the-company-tent.title: The Company Tent
the-company-tent.intro: A good tent, the only one in the camp with a floor. Ink, wet canvas, and from the yard behind it, lime. The company man sits at a folding desk under a painted sign: a barge, a handbell, a hand. He smiles at everyone the same.{if [q:crisis-claim-talk] > 0} Since the news there's a line at his desk that goes out of the tent, and he smiles at all of it.{/if}

branches.title: Work a shift in the dead-yard
branches.description: Work a shift in the dead-yard: mucking out, mending, carrying what the dead can't be trusted with.

success.title: Two coin, and a good shift
success.description: You shovel lime over what the dead leave behind, mend a fence they leaned on, and carry water past rows of them standing in the yard, waiting for a bell. Two coin at the end, counted into your hand, and the company man chalks a mark against your name: a good shift. The smell comes with you.

failure.title: Half a shift
failure.description: Half a shift of posts goes into your arms and stays there. Then one slips while you're carrying it and opens your palm. The yard-keeper pays you for half a shift and tells you to wrap the hand before it festers. One coin.

branches.title: Work a shift beside the young man
branches.description: Stand in the yard line beside [who:young-man], so the company man takes you both, and work the shift together. He'll need you to take the heavy end.

success.title: Two marks on the board
success.description: You take the heavy end of every post and every barrow, and he takes the light end and talks, and between you it gets done. When he coughs, you carry. When the company man looks over, he stands up straight. Two coin each at the end, and two chalk marks on the board. "There," he says. "Told you we'd pass."

failure.title: Half a shift each
failure.description: Your back takes his share of the weight as well as yours, and it'll be the stronger for it. Halfway through, he goes grey and sits down on a barrow, and you can't carry for two. The yard-keeper pays you both for half a shift, and you've a cut on your hand from a post you held too long. "Next time," he says. "Next time I'll carry you."

branches.title: Sign your death to the company
branches.description: Sign your death to the company. They pay you for it.
branches.hoverText: The company will own your body when you die, and work it until it falls apart. It brands its mark on your brow, and the gate won't read it for three nights. You can't take it back.

success.title: Welcome to the company
success.description:
He reads it out to you, kindly: on your death, your body to the company, for its use, until worn. You put your cross on the paper. He counts two coin into your hand and hangs a seal round your neck: barge, handbell, hand.

Then the yard-keeper takes an iron out of the fire pan, and the company man holds your head still himself. The brand goes on your brow, where the nail will go. "Welcome," he says, through the smell of it, "to the company. We look after our own."

branches.title: Go round to the yard's back gate
branches.description: Go round behind the tent to the yard's back gate, where the lantern is.

success.title: The back gate
success.description: The lane behind the tent is mud and lime. Somewhere in the yard, a handbell, once.

the-criers-offer.title: The Crier's Offer
the-criers-offer.intro: The company's crier is up on his cart again, calling for hands. This time his eye stops on you, and he smiles like a man who has seen you before. "Still here," he says. "Long enough to be hungry, then. The company has work."{if [q:claim] >= 1} He glances at the seal on your cord. "That won't feed you."{/if}

branches.title: Ask him what the work is
branches.description: Ask him what the work is, and what it pays.

success.title: Two coin a shift
success.description: "Shifts in the dead-yard, for the living. Two coin a shift, counted into your hand." He points past his cart, to a big tent with the company's sign over the door, and the yard's fence behind it. "Ask inside. And when you're tired of being hungry, the man in there will talk to you about a seal."

branches.title: Tell him you're not signing anything
branches.description: Tell him you're not signing anything. Not your death, not today.

success.title: Nobody's asking
success.description: "Nobody's asking you to sign," he says, still smiling. "Not today. The yard wants hands, that's all." He points past his cart, to a big tent with the company's sign over the door. "Two coin a shift. Ask inside, when you're hungry enough."

the-dead-go-out.title: The Dead Go Out
the-dead-go-out.intro:
Morning. The yard gate swings open and the dead go out to work: a column three wide, with their drovers beside it, each ringing a handbell at every step. They walk in time, pewter seals nailed to their brows.

[who:regard-rope-mother] has put the haulers' bucket in your hand: the pot wants water. The well is on the other side of the road.

branches.title: Cross through the column
branches.description: Cross through the column to the well. They won't touch you. Probably.

success.title: Close enough to read
success.description:
You step between two of them, close enough to smell lime and old meat. Close enough to read the seals: a chapel, a barge, a barge, a barge. One woman's seal has a child's name scratched in round the nail.

Then you're through, at the well, and you can't make your hands stop shaking.

failure.title: A head turns
failure.description: You get one step in among them, and your nerve is the harder for it. Then one of them turns its head. Only that: a head turning, slow, to look at nothing. You're back on the near side before you know you moved. The column goes on, and the nearest drover laughs. You fetch the water when the road is empty, and the pot is late.

branches.title: Walk through them
branches.description: Walk through them to the well. They don't frighten you. You know what's under every one of those nails, and how little it takes to hold them.

success.title: You know what holds them
success.description: You walk between them the way you'd walk between cattle. Close enough to read the seals: a chapel, a barge, a barge, a barge. One woman's seal has a child's name scratched in round the nail. Behind you, someone in the camp says a word under their breath. It isn't a kind one.

branches.title: Wait for them to pass
branches.description: Wait for them to pass. It takes a while.

success.title: Two hundred, give or take
success.description: Two hundred, give or take. You lose count at a hundred and twelve, when a dead boy goes by no taller than your chest. Each drover counts their own, out loud, by the bell. One stops at six; another is still counting when the rest have finished. Then the road is empty, and you fetch the water.

the-dues-round.title: The Dues Round
the-dues-round.intro: [who:regard-rope-mother] gets up off her coil in stages, the box hugged to her chest, and stands a moment getting her breath back. "Dues night," she says. She looks down at the box, then at you. "Heavier every year, this. Or I'm lighter."

branches.title: Carry the box for her
branches.description: Take the box from her, and carry it round the fires.

success.title: Round the fires
success.description: You take the box.

branches.title: Leave her to it
branches.description: Leave her to it. It's her box.

success.title: Her own box
success.description: She tucks it under her arm and sets off along the fires, slowly, stopping to rest at every one. It's full dark before she's back, and she sits down without a word.

the-fleet-is-lost.title: The Fleet Is Lost

branches.title: Go back to the fire
branches.description: Go back to the haulers' fire.

success.title: The fire
success.description: You go back.

the-haulers-fire.title: The Haulers' Fire
the-haulers-fire.intro: The haulers' fire, on the dry side of the camp. Canvas, coils of rope nobody uses any more, and a big black pot.{if [q:presence-rope-mother] == 1} [who:regard-rope-mother] sits on a coil with her pipe, watching the road, her feet on a small iron-bound box.{/if}{if [q:presence-young-man] == 1}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] <= 1} [who:young-man] sits on the log nearby, coughing into his sleeve.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] == 2} [who:young-man] sits as close to the flames as he can get, sweating and shivering at once.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] >= 3} [who:young-man] lies by the fire under a blanket, and doesn't sit up.{/if}{/if}{if [q:prologue] >= 4}{if [q:prologue-bound-the-young-man] > 0 && [q:prologue-released-the-young-man] == 0 && [q:prologue-hired-out-the-young-man] == 0} [who:young-man] stands at the edge of the firelight, waiting. The haulers keep their backs to him.{else} [who:young-man]'s place on the log is empty.{/if}{/if}{if [q:crisis-claim-talk] > 0} The talk round the fire is all of bread by the claim, and who will get it.{/if}{if [q:chill] >= 1} You hold your hands to the flames, close enough to scorch your cuffs, and they stay cold.{/if}

branches.title: Eat from your provisions
branches.description: Eat from your provisions, here by the fire.

success.title: Bread and an onion
success.description: Bread, an onion, a heel of cheese. Hot water from the pot to wash it down. The fire does the rest.

branches.title: Sit and talk
branches.description: Sit down by [who:regard-rope-mother], and talk.

success.title: A word at the fire
success.description: She shifts along the coil to make room.

branches.title: Sit with the young man
branches.description: Sit down on the log by [who:young-man].

success.title: On the log
success.description: He makes room.

branches.title: The young man you bound
branches.description: Go to [who:young-man]. He's yours, now.

success.title: He waits
success.description: He turns his head when you come close.

branches.title: A blanket from the dead-yard
branches.description: {if [time:day] >= 2}At first light, four haulers come up from the dead-yard with a blanket between them, and the whole fire gets to its feet.{else}Four haulers are coming up from the dead-yard with a blanket between them. One by one, the people at the fire get to their feet.{/if} Go and see who it is.

success.title: One of ours
success.description: You go to see.

branches.title: Join the burial club
branches.description: Ask [who:regard-rope-mother] to put your name in her book. [c:club-fee] coin into the box to join, then [c:club-dues] every [c:club-dues-every] days, and the club holds your death.
branches.hoverText: The burial club will hold your death, and its binder will release you at once: nobody works your body. The rope-mother pricks the club's knot into your wrist, and the gate won't read it for three nights. Then the dues come every few days, for as long as you live out here. Miss them, and you're out, and what you paid stays in the box.

success.title: Into the book
success.description:
She counts your coin into the box, opens the book on her knee, and writes your name under the last one, slowly, with her tongue between her teeth. Then she takes a seal out of her own pocket, a knot stamped deep, and hangs it round your neck herself. She blackens a sail needle in the fire, and pricks the same knot into the inside of your wrist, where a rope would sit. It takes the rest of her pipe.

"When you go, nobody works you. Not a day." She shuts the book. "[c:club-dues] coin, every [c:club-dues-every] days. Miss it, and you're out, and what you paid stays in the box."

branches.title: Forage along the river
branches.description: Go down to the river with a bucket, and see what it gives today: the traps, the cress beds, the stones below the rapids.

success.title: A full bucket
success.description: An eel in the third trap, cress past the mills, and a bucket of mussels from the far shallows, where the current tugs at your knees. You come back up the steps wet to the thighs and numb with cold, with the bucket full.

failure.title: Thin pickings
failure.description: You know the river a little better for the day it gave you: where the water is slow, where nobody else has been. Today it gave you nothing much.
