Somebody has been at the traps before you, and the cress beds are picked over. A handful of mussels, wet legs, and the long climb back up the steps.

branches.title: Sit up with the camp's dead
branches.description: Sit up through the night with the camp's dead, by the chapel wall, with your weapon across your knees.

success.title: Two coin at first light
success.description: Towards the small hours, one of the shapes under the sacking moves. Then it sits up. You're on your feet before it is, and you hit it at the head, and again, until it lies down for good. Nobody in the tents wakes. At first light the haulers pay you two coin, and you sleep a little, sitting up against the wall.

success.title: A quiet night
success.description: Nothing under the sacking moves all night. The rats do, and the cold does, and twice you're sure, and you're wrong. You sit with your weapon across your knees until the sky goes grey and the carts come. Two coin from the haulers at first light, and then sleep, at last, with your back to the cold stones.

failure.title: Teeth
failure.description: You'll be quicker next time; your arm learns from a night like this. Towards the small hours one of them sits up, and you're slow, and it gets hold of your arm with its teeth before you put it down. At first light the haulers pay you one coin, for half a watch, and look at your arm. You sleep badly against the wall, with the bite throbbing.

branches.title: Sit up with the camp's dead, the pistol loaded
branches.description: Load the pistol with the watch's one charge, and sit up through the night with the camp's dead, by the chapel wall.

success.title: One shot
success.description: Towards the small hours, one of the shapes under the sacking moves. Then it sits up. You wind the lock, and wait until it turns its face to you, and fire once. The whole camp wakes, and then goes back to sleep. At first light the haulers pay you two coin, and take back the horn. You sleep a little, with the smell of powder still on your hands.

success.title: The charge unfired
success.description: Nothing under the sacking moves all night. You sit with the pistol wound and the charge in it, and your thumb on the lock, until the sky goes grey and the carts come. At first light you draw the charge and give it back, and the haulers pay you two coin. Then a little sleep, sitting up, with your back to the wall.

failure.title: A miss in the dark
failure.description: Your hands will be steadier with the lock next time; this night taught them. Towards the small hours one of them sits up. You fire too soon, in the dark, and miss, and it's on you before you can turn the pistol round to club it. You put it down in the end, with your arm bitten to the bone. At first light the haulers pay you one coin, for half a watch. You sleep in the end, with your arm wrapped in your shirt.

branches.title: Change your clothes
branches.description: Change your clothes behind the haulers' canvas.

success.title: Behind the canvas
success.description: You duck behind the canvas.

branches.title: Sleep by the fire
branches.description: Roll up by the fire, and sleep.

success.title: The fire burns down
success.description: The fire burns down. The dead-yard's lanterns don't. Once, in the dark, a handbell rings in the yard, and a great many feet shuffle, and stop.

branches.title: Too cold to sleep
branches.description: On your feet you could ignore it. Lying still on the wet ground, the cold comes up into you. Sit in close to the fire until it's out of your bones.

success.title: Half the night
success.description: You sit with your knees to the embers and feed the fire what the haulers will spare: bark, a split oar, a rope's end. Somewhere past midnight the cold lets go. You sleep where you sit, and wake stiff, with your chin on your chest.

branches.title: Buy wood for the fire
branches.description: A boy goes round the fires with a sack of split wood, a coin an armful. Enough to keep this one in most of the night.

success.title: Kept in
success.description: The boy bites your coin before he tips the wood out. Nobody at the fire thanks you; they just shift closer. Most of the night someone feeds it, and the cold stays on the far side of the flames. For once, you sleep the whole night through.

branches.title: Too shaken to sleep
branches.description: Every time you shut your eyes, it's there again. The haulers are sitting up{if [q:prologue-release-today] > 0} for the old man{/if}. Sit up with them till it passes.

success.title: Till it passes
success.description: Nobody asks what's wrong with you. {if [q:prologue-release-today] > 0}They talk about the old man: the drowned ox he pulled out of the river by its horns, and what he said to the company man the day they took the towpath.{else}They talk about the river, and the price of bread, and nothing much.{/if} Somewhere in the talk your hands stop shaking. You sleep sitting up, and wake with a crick in your neck.

branches.title: Share the haulers' jug
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 10}The jug goes round, and the haulers drink to what they've seen. You pass it on. You always do.{else}The jug goes round for whoever puts something in the pot for the morning. Put in a loaf, and drink until you stop seeing it.{/if}

success.title: Under
success.description: Your bread goes in the pot. The ale is thin and sour, and there's plenty of it. The fire swims, the haulers' talk goes soft at the edges, and the next thing you know it's grey morning and somebody is stepping over you. Your mouth tastes of the jug, and your head rings like the chapel bell.

the-land-gate.title: The Land Gate
the-land-gate.intro: The land gate: a tunnel through a wall ten paces thick, its stones black with age at the bottom and newer above, where the dead built it higher. Wardens in red under the arch. Cold air breathes out of it, smelling of the city.{if [time:bell] > 3} At this hour the arrivals' door is shut, and people sleep against the wall to be first in the morning.{/if}

branches.title: Watch who gets through
branches.description: Stand by the arch for an hour, and watch who gets through, and how.
branches.hoverText: The arrivals' door is open from Prime to Sext.

success.title: Marks
success.description:
Company brands first, on the brow, a barge and a handbell and a hand burned where the nail will go. The wardens barely look at them. Church marks get a hand turned to the light, and a name asked. A man in a fur collar holds up a seal on a gold chain, and they bow him through without touching his hands at all. A man with no mark is walked back down the road by his elbow.

And one warden, a thin one with a broken nose, waves the burial club's knots through without looking at them.

branches.title: Talk to the people sleeping by the wall
branches.description: Sit down by the people sleeping against the wall, and ask how the gate works.

success.title: Days of watching
success.description: A woman with a baby has been here four days. "Company brand walks straight in," she says. "Church mark, they read your hand and ask your name. Nothing on you, they walk you down the road. Something new on you, they make you wait till it heals." She nods at the shut door. "There's a thin one with a broken nose does the mornings. He lets the burial club's knots by without a look. Don't know why. Wish I had one."

branches.title: Go in
branches.description: Hold out your hands, and your mark, and go in.
branches.hoverText: The gate takes arrivals from Prime to Sext, and only with a claim: a mark the wardens can read. A fresh mark takes three nights to heal.

success.title: Through
success.description: The warden reaches for your hands.

the-late-barge-continues.title: The Late Barge Continues
the-late-barge-continues.intro: The Late Barge continues in a later build. The prologue ends here.

branches.title: Wait
branches.description: Wait, for now.

success.title: Time passes
success.description: Time passes. The bells ring it out.

branches.title: Find somewhere to sleep
branches.description: Find a doorway, a stair, a church porch: somewhere out of the wind.

success.title: A doorway out of the wind
success.description: You curl up in a church porch with your back to the door.

the-list-at-the-chapel-door.title: The List at the Chapel Door
the-list-at-the-chapel-door.intro: Four hand-carts at the chapel door this morning, and a line beside them for the list nailed up there: the camp's dead that nobody came for. At noon they go to the law. When you came, the list was half a page. Now it's two. Most of the line can't read.{if [q:prologue-saw-the-release] + [q:prologue-rope-mother-told-club] > 0} At the haulers' fire they say the burial box pays out twice a week now, and the dues have gone up.{/if}

branches.title: Read the names out for the people in the line
branches.description: {if [q:origin] == 6}You've read lists like this aloud before, in a cold church, for people who couldn't. Read the names out for the line.{else}Stand on the step, and read the names out for the people in the line.{/if}

success.title: Every name
success.description:
You read every name, slowly, and twice when they ask. Halfway down the second page a woman hears the one she came for, and sits down in the mud without a sound. The line closes round her.

When you finish, [who:regard-binder] is standing in the chapel door. She nods to you, once, and goes back to the carts.

failure.title: Somebody takes over
failure.description: The letters come quicker the longer you read; you're better at this than when you started. But the names are badly written and worse spelled, and you stumble on one, then another, and the line gets restless. A clerk from the chapel takes the list down and reads it out in a flat voice, faster than you could.

branches.title: Help the carters push the hand-carts up to the door
branches.description: The carters are short of hands. Help them push the hand-carts up the last of the hill to the chapel door.

success.title: A coin a cart
success.description: Four carts, and something under a sack on each. One of the sacks has a hand hanging out of it, small, with a ring of plaited grass on one finger. Nobody tucks it back in. The carters give you a coin when the last cart is at the door, and don't say thank you. It isn't that kind of work.

branches.title: Walk on
branches.description: Walk on. There's nothing on that list for you.

success.title: Not your name
success.description: You walk on. Behind you, someone in the line is reading the names out, badly, a word at a time. You hear them all the way down the hill.

the-man-who-saves.title: The Man Who Saves
the-man-who-saves.intro: {if [q:prologue-sat-with-the-saver] + [q:prologue-told-the-saver-about-the-club] == 0}A man in a heavy coat sits against a tent pole in the full sun, fighting to keep his eyes open. The coat is good wool, too good for out here, and lumpy at the seams. When he shifts it chinks, and he goes still until it stops. "Sit by me while I sleep," he says. "Can't sleep at night. Not out here." He holds up a coin.{else}The man in the heavy coat is in the same place, in the sun, his chin dropping onto his chest. He sees you and lifts a hand, with a coin already in it.{/if}

branches.title: Sit by him while he sleeps
branches.description: Sit down with your back to his, and watch the road while he sleeps.

success.title: Back to back
success.description: {if [q:prologue-sat-with-the-saver] <= 1}He talks until he sleeps: a binder's price, [c:release-price] coin, to let himself go when it comes. Eleven years he's been sewing it into the coat, a coin at a time. Then he's asleep, and you sit two bells in the sun and watch the road. When he wakes he pays you, and runs his fingers down every seam before he says thank you.{else}Two bells in the sun, back to back, while he sleeps like a dropped sack. Nobody comes near. When he wakes he pays you, and runs his fingers down every seam before he says anything at all.{/if}

branches.title: Sit by him, and cut a seam while he sleeps
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 6}All that coin, sewn into one coat, on a man who can't stay awake. Sit by him, and when he sleeps, cut a seam.{else}Sit by him as if to watch, and when he's asleep, cut one seam of the coat.{/if}

success.title: One seam
success.description: He sleeps like the dead. Your knife goes in along the hem, and coin comes out into your palm, warm from him, and you close the seam with your thumb so it hangs right. Nobody at the nearest fire says anything. But a woman there watched you sit down beside him, and she watches you go.

failure.title: He wakes
failure.description: Your fingers will be quicker next time; they're learning the work. This time he wakes with your knife in his hem, and screams like a gull. Half the tents round about turn out to see. You're gone before they're on their feet, but they all saw your back, and some of them saw your face.

branches.title: Tell him about the burial club
branches.description: Tell him about [who:regard-rope-mother]'s box, and the book of names.

success.title: A coin every few days
success.description: He listens with his eyes shut, his hand flat on his coat. "[c:club-dues] coin every few days," he says, "for as long as I live. And if I miss once, it's gone." He opens his eyes. "I've never missed once. Not in eleven years." He doesn't say no. He doesn't say yes. He goes to sleep.

branches.title: Walk on
branches.description: Leave him to stay awake on his own, and walk on.

success.title: Further down
success.description: You walk on, further down. When you look back he's still sitting up against the pole, his eyes open as wide as he can make them.

the-nights-watch.title: The Night's Watch
the-nights-watch.intro:
The haulers are making up the night's watch. Two of the camp's dead lie by the chapel wall under sacking, waiting for the morning carts, and another one by the far fires. Nobody holds them. If one gets up in the night, somebody has to put it down before it gets in among the tents.

"Each fire puts in a coin," [who:regard-rope-mother] says. "Two for whoever sits up with them." She looks at what you carry. "You've a weapon."

branches.title: Show them how you hold it
branches.description: Show them how you hold it, and what you'd do with it.

success.title: On the list
success.description: You show them the blow that ends one: hard, at the head, and again. Nobody laughs. She puts your name on the watch, after the two haulers who keep it most nights. "Sit up with them when you like," she says. "Come to the fire after dark."

failure.title: The dead don't care
failure.description: Your grip is better for the showing, and your arm knows the swing a little better. It still isn't much. One of the haulers laughs. [who:regard-rope-mother] doesn't. "The dead don't care how pretty it looks," she says. "Hit the head, and hit it twice. Come to the fire after dark, when you want a night."

branches.title: Show them the pistol
branches.description: Show them the pistol. It isn't loaded, and you say so.

success.title: A charge a night
success.description: One of the haulers whistles. [who:regard-rope-mother] goes into the canvas and comes back with a cow's horn of powder and a bag of shot no bigger than a fist. "The watch keeps this for the one with the gun," she says. "One charge a night. What you don't fire, you give back." She puts your name on the watch. "Come to the fire after dark."

the-old-city.title: The Old City
the-old-city.intro:
Bells. Every church in the city at once, ringing the hour, and under them, from every street, the drovers' handbells answering.

Wet stone, fish, smoke, and people: more people than you've seen in your life, in streets built for a quarter of them. Above the roofs, the cathedral, black with age. Beside it, a round brick building with a dome, newer, with a queue at its door. Below, the river, white over the rapids, and the mills turning on it, and the dead walking the wheels.

branches.title: Go up to the domed building
branches.description: Go up to the round building with the dome, and see what the queue is for.

success.title: The anatomy theatre
success.description:
The anatomy theatre. Pilgrims in one line, students in another, a door for each. Over the doors, a statue of a thin figure in a gown, holding up a nail the way saints hold up their relics.

Someone has scratched a word into the stone at its feet, and someone else has tried to scrub it out. You can still read it: BUTCHER.

branches.title: Go down to the river
branches.description: Go down to the river, where the crowd is thickest.

success.title: The grain docks
success.description: The grain docks: stone berths for twenty barges, and every one of them empty. Merchants' men stand at the warehouse doors with their arms folded. Carts come out of the warehouses full and go up into the city, and the bread queue at the river gate goes round the corner and out of sight.

the-old-clothes-seller.title: The Old-Clothes Seller
the-old-clothes-seller.intro: Between the onion woman and the knife-grinder, a woman sells clothes off a rope strung between two poles. Good wool, a lace cuff, a pair of boots with the soles still on. Nobody asks where they come from. Everyone knows: the yards take the dead in their skins, and somebody sells what is left.

branches.title: A wool cap
branches.description: Grey wool, mended at the top. 4 coin.

success.title: A wool cap
success.description: She bites the coin, and tosses you the cap. It fits well enough.

branches.title: Fingerless gloves
branches.description: Knitted, with the thumbs worn through. 6 coin.

success.title: Fingerless gloves
success.description: She counts the coins twice, then pegs the next pair where the gloves hung.

branches.title: A phial of rose water
branches.description: Stoppered with wax, and half full. 12 coin.

success.title: A phial of rose water
success.description: She sniffs the phial before she hands it over, as if to check it is still roses.

branches.title: A drover's oilcloth cape
branches.description: Black, waxed, and long enough to sit on. 18 coin.

success.title: A drover's oilcloth cape
success.description: She unpegs the cape, shakes the dust off, and drapes it over your arm.

branches.title: A dyed sash
branches.description: A colour from somewhere else. 20 coin.

success.title: A dyed sash
success.description: She winds the sash round her own hand once, then hands it over with a sigh.

branches.title: A broad hat with a feather
branches.description: Black felt, and one long dyed feather. 35 coin.

success.title: A broad hat with a feather
success.description: She sets the hat on your head herself, and tilts it. "There."

branches.title: A merchant's doublet
branches.description: Slashed sleeves, lined with red silk. 45 coin.

success.title: A merchant's doublet
success.description: She counts the coins slowly, out loud, so the row can hear. Then the doublet is yours.

branches.title: A silver mourning ring
branches.description: Silver, with a small skull on top. 60 coin.

success.title: A silver mourning ring
success.description: She polishes the ring on her apron, and drops it in your palm. "Wear it in good health."

the-old-drain.title: The Old Drain
the-old-drain.intro: Below the tanneries the wall goes down into the river mud, and there's a hole in it the size of a barrel: the old drain. It smells of every year the city has stood. If it comes up anywhere, it comes up inside the walls. If you don't drown.

branches.title: Go in through the drain
branches.description: Duck under the lip of the hole, and feel your way in.

success.title: Behind the dyer's
success.description: Black water to the knees, then to the waist, then a grating that lifts when you put your back into it. You come up in an alley behind a dyer's, filthy, inside the walls, with nobody's mark on you.

failure.title: A lantern
failure.description: You go further into the dark than most would dare, and quieter; the dark will be easier next time. Then a lantern swings out over the drain mouth. A warden on the bank, with his hand out. You put a coin in it, if you have one. He puts the lantern away. "Mornings," he says. "Through the gate. With a mark. Like a decent soul."

branches.title: Not into that
branches.description: Not now. Not into that.

success.title: Back up the bank
success.description: You climb back up the bank. The drain will be there tomorrow. So will the smell.

the-road-in.title: The Road In
the-road-in.intro:
Bells first, before the walls. One deep church bell somewhere above, and under it, from the fields on both sides of the road, a scatter of small bells answering it.

Then the smell: river mud, tanneries, smoke. Then the city, on its rock above the rapids. The road narrows into a queue for the gate: carts, walkers, a priest on a mule, dust on everyone.

Ahead, a bound dead man hauls a cart up the hill, harnessed like an ox, the seal of his binding nailed to his brow. His drover walks beside him ringing a handbell, and the dead man's feet keep time.

"Fleet's late," says the carter behind you, to nobody. "Grain should've been up the river a week since. Bread's up a penny already."

Up at the arch, wardens in red look every arrival over. A family comes back down against the queue, the father pulling his cuff down over a bare wrist.

branches.title: Walk on to the gate
branches.description: Pull your scarf up against the dust, and shuffle on toward the arch with everyone else.

success.title: To the gate
success.description: The queue moves a step at a time.

the-round-of-the-fires.title: Round the Fires
the-round-of-the-fires.intro:
The box is heavier than it looks. She walks ahead of you with the book and a stub of charcoal, and at every fire somebody is waiting for her.

A washerwoman counts coppers out of a knotted rag, two of them twice, and asks to see the mark made. A porter pays for himself and for his mother, asleep under a cart, who hasn't paid her own in a year. Two brothers from the mills argue over whose turn it is, and the younger one pays. A man nobody seems to know pays for next time as well, and watches you carry it away.

At the tanners' fire she takes nothing. She kneels by a woman under a blanket and holds her hand a while, and says something too low to hear. Then she gets up, knees cracking. "Not yet," she says, to you or to the woman, and walks on.

branches.title: Go on to the last fire
branches.description: Go on to the last fire, by the mill race.

success.title: The last fire
success.description: You go on.

the-surgeons-awning.title: The Surgeon's Awning
the-surgeons-awning.intro: An awning of old sailcloth by the road, a table under it scrubbed white, and a basin of water going pink.{if [q:met-surgeon] == 0} A man in a leather apron is rinsing his hands. Beside him a roll of knives lies open, small to large, very clean, and a painted board leans on the post: a man with his skin off, every muscle named.{else} [who:surgeon] looks up from the basin, and at the wound before your face.{/if}

branches.title: Have the cut stitched
branches.description: Have him stitch the cut. Two coin, and he's quick.

success.title: Six stitches
success.description: He washes it out with something that burns worse than the cut, and closes it with six stitches, small and even. He talks the whole time about what lies under the skin there, which cord does what, as if you'd asked. "[who:surgeon]," he says, tying off. "Two coin. Keep it dry."

branches.title: Pay him to see to it properly
branches.description: Pay him to see to it properly: cut out what's bad, and close what's left. Four coin, and he wants to see a seal first.

success.title: On the table
success.description:
He reads your seal before he looks at the wound. Then he lays you on the table, cuts away what has gone bad, and sews what's left, quick and neat. The pain goes white, then grey. When you can sit up he is rinsing his knives.

"[who:surgeon]. Four coin. You'll live. And if you don't, somebody comes for you."

branches.title: Show him the wound, and ask
branches.description: Show him the wound, and ask him to see to it.

success.title: No seal
success.description:
He looks at the wound, and then at your neck, where a seal should hang. "Not on my table," he says. "If you die there with no seal on you, nobody comes for you. You lie there till you get up." He dries his hands. "[who:surgeon]. Come back with a seal."

Then, lower: "Or go round to the back of the company's yard after the dead come in. The yard-keeper sews anything. He's had the practice."

the-wardens.title: The Wardens
the-wardens.intro:
The morning is half gone before you reach the arch. The wardens are bored, leaning on halberds, red coats grey with dust. Every arrival holds out their hands, and a warden takes them in his own and holds them a moment, like a man feeling for a fever.

The woman in front of you holds hers out. The warden lets go fast. "Licence," he says. She shows him a paper with a seal. He waves her through, and wipes his palms on his coat.

Your turn.

branches.title: Hold out your hands
branches.description: Hold out your hands. Warm, and nothing to hide in them.

success.title: Mark?
success.description:
He holds them, turns them over, looks at the backs and then at your brow, and lets go. "Mark." You don't know what he means. He pushes back his cuff: a tower, pricked in ink into his wrist, the council's. A pewter seal with the same tower hangs at his neck.

"Mark," he says again, slower. "Who holds your death?"

Nobody does.

"Then you don't come in. Nobody dies in here without someone to answer for the body." He jerks his thumb down the road. "Camp's below. Gate takes arrivals in the mornings." He's already looking past you.

branches.title: Hide that you can bind
branches.description: Some arrivals rub their hands warm against their thighs before the warden reaches them. Yours are warm already.
branches.hoverText: In another life… maybe.

success.title: He lets go
success.description:
He holds them a breath longer than the last pair, and turns them over to look at the backs. Then he lets go. "Mark."

You have none. You don't even know what he means until he pushes back his cuff: a tower, pricked in ink into his wrist, the council's.

"Then you don't come in. Camp's below. Gate takes arrivals in the mornings."

You walk away with your hands in your armpits. They're cold again before you reach the bottom of the road.

failure.title: He feels it
failure.description:
Your face holds still, even while your hands give you away. He feels it. You watch him feel it: the cold coming up through the warmth you rubbed in. He looks at your face for a long time, learning it.

"No licence," he says, quietly. "No mark either, I see." You have none. "Camp's below. Gate takes arrivals in the mornings."

He doesn't call anyone. He doesn't need to. He'll remember you.

the-wound.title: The Wound
the-wound.intro:
{if [q:wounds-festering] > 0}The wound has gone hot under the rag. It's red a hand's width round, and it smells sweet, the way meat does on the second day.{else}{if [q:wounds] >= 3}The wound pulls every time you move, and the rag on it is brown through. People in the lanes look at it, then at you.{else}The cut throbs under its rag. Clean, for now. Nothing stays clean for long in a camp this crowded.{/if}{/if}{if [q:origin] == 3} You've seen men lose an arm to less.{/if}{if [q:origin] == 1} At home your mother put cobwebs on a cut, and there are plenty here.{/if}{if [q:origin] == 6} The sisters who kept the sick-room boiled every rag twice. You remember that much.{/if}{if [q:met-surgeon] == 0}

There's a surgeon under an awning by the road, people say, for anyone with coin.{/if}

branches.title: Clean it and bind it
branches.description: {if [q:wounds-festering] > 0}Open it up again, clean out what's gone bad, and bind it tight. It's going to hurt.{else}Beg hot water from a cook-fire, wash the cut out, and bind it tight.{/if}

success.title: Clean
success.description: The water's too hot and you use it anyway. You pick the wound clean with a pin, whatever's in it, and bind it tight with the cleanest rag you own. It stings for an hour, and then it only aches, which is better.

failure.title: Heat in it
failure.description: Your hands learn the shape of a wound, and they'll be steadier for it. But the rag was never as clean as it looked. Before long there's heat in the wound, spreading, and a sweet smell when you lift the binding.

branches.title: Wrap it and leave it
branches.description: Wrap it and leave it be. Most wounds close by themselves. Most.

success.title: It closes
success.description: You keep it wrapped and keep it dry, as well as anyone can here. By the next bell it has stopped weeping. It will scar, if it's that kind.

success.title: It festers
success.description: You wrap it and get on with things. The rag stays on too long. Under it the wound goes hot and red, and starts to smell sweet.

success.title: It drains
success.description: You leave it. Later it breaks and drains by itself, foul, and the fever goes out of you with it. You know that was luck.

success.title: It spreads
success.description: You leave it. The red creeps out from under the rag, a finger's width at a time, and your head swims when you stand up too fast.

branches.title: Let the woman from the next tent dress it
branches.description: A woman from the next tent has watched you favour it. She has clean linen, a needle, three children, and no bread.

success.title: Bread for her children
success.description: She washes it with water she has boiled twice, and sews it with thread from her own hem, quick and small. "Bread," she says when she's done, and holds out her hand. Her children watch the loaf all the way to her.

the-yards-back-gate.title: The Yard's Back Gate
the-yards-back-gate.intro: {if [q:met-yard-keeper] == 0}Behind the company tent, a gate in the fence, and lantern light. The dead stand in their rows in the yard, still as posts. By the gate a man with a cloth tied over his face is sewing up a dead woman's forearm with sailcloth thread. She holds the arm out for him, patient as a horse being shod. He doesn't look up. "Surgeon sent you?"{else}The back gate, the lantern, the rows of the dead. [who:regard-yard-keeper] sits at his trestle with a needle between his teeth{if [q:regard-yard-keeper] >= 1}, and nods you to the lantern hook{/if}.{/if}

branches.title: Pay him to stitch it
branches.description: Pay him a coin to stitch it.

success.title: The same thread
success.description: He finishes the dead woman's arm first. Then he washes his hands in a bucket of lime-water, and sews you shut with the same thread, in the same small stitches. "[who:regard-yard-keeper]," he says, and holds out his hand for the coin. "You flinch. They don't."

branches.title: Hold the lantern while he works
branches.description: Hold the lantern for him while he works down the row, and he'll see to you after.

success.title: Down the row
success.description:
You hold the lantern while he works down the row: a split hand, a jaw tied shut, a foot turned the wrong way. He names each thing as he does it, to the dead or to you. Your nerve holds. At the end he sits you on the trestle and does you the same way.

"[who:regard-yard-keeper]," he says. "Come back if you want work. The pay's poor, and the company's quiet."

failure.title: A head turns to the light
failure.description: You hold the lantern down the row, and your nerve is the harder for every one of them. Then a dead man turns his head to the light, slow, and you have to set the lantern down and walk away a while. When you come back, [who:regard-yard-keeper] sews you up without a word, and doesn't ask you to hold anything.

branches.title: Tell him you've no coin to spare
branches.description: Tell him you've no coin to spare.

success.title: His book
success.description: "No coin." He wipes his hands, takes a book from inside his coat, and writes in it with a stub of lead: your name, and something in a column beside it that you can't read upside down. Then he sews you up as neatly as he sewed her. "[who:regard-yard-keeper]," he says. "No charge."

branches.title: Watch him work a while
branches.description: There's nothing left to sew. Watch him work a while.

success.title: Nothing to sew
success.description: "Nothing to sew, then." He works on, and lets you watch: the thread drawn tight, the skin pulled straight, the dead woman holding still the whole time. "[who:regard-yard-keeper]," he says at last. "Come back when you're bleeding."

branches.title: Have him stitch it
branches.description: Have him stitch it. A coin.

success.title: Small, tight stitches
success.description: He sits you on the trestle among the dead and sews you shut in small, tight stitches, while the one he was working on waits with its arm out. A coin, and he's back to it before you're on your feet.

branches.title: Hold the lantern for him, for pay
branches.description: Hold the lantern for him down the rows, for pay.

success.title: Two coin, and aching eyes
success.description: Two bells with the lantern, down the rows: a split heel, a cheek sewn back on, a hand wired to its wrist. He names what he does as he does it. Two coin at the end, and your eyes ache from the light.

failure.title: Steadier tomorrow
failure.description: Two bells with the lantern, and your nerve is the harder for every one. Near the end a dead boy's eyes follow the light, and the lantern shakes so much that he takes it from you. One coin. "Steadier tomorrow," he says.

branches.title: Leave him to it
branches.description: Leave him to it.

success.title: Back to the camp
success.description: He doesn't look up from his needle.

the-young-man-waits.title: He Waits
the-young-man-waits.intro: {if [q:prologue-hired-out-the-young-man] > 0}[who:young-man] comes out of the company's yard when the drover rings him out, mud to the knees, and stands in front of you. He waits for you to tell him something.{else}[who:young-man] stands where you left him, at the edge of the firelight, his eyes on you. His face is still his face. He coughs, once, out of habit, though there's no breath in it. He waits for you to tell him something.{/if}

branches.title: Let him go
branches.description: Put your cold hands on his face, and let him go.
branches.hoverText: Unbinding costs nothing. He will lie still for good.

success.title: Done
success.description:
You draw out the nail, and that's all it takes. [who:young-man] folds down onto the grass like a coat dropped off a peg, and lies still.

Behind you, [who:regard-rope-mother] lets out a breath. "There," she says. "There. Now he's done."

branches.title: Hire him to the company yard
branches.description: Walk him to the company tent. The company man rents bound hands by the day.
branches.hoverText: The company pays you 2 coin each morning while you're in the camp and he works in their yard.

success.title: Two coin a day
success.description:
The company man walks round him once, and looks at his teeth. "Young. Sound. He'll do two years in the mill-yard, if you look after the nail." He counts out two coin. "Same again every morning he's in our yard. We'll ring him out for you when you want him."

[who:young-man] walks into the yard with the others, and doesn't look back.

branches.title: Leave him as he is
branches.description: Leave him as he is, for now.

success.title: Waiting
success.description: You turn away. When you look back, he's still watching you.

the-young-mans-cough.title: His Cough
the-young-mans-cough.intro: {if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] <= 1}[who:young-man]'s cough woke half the fire before dawn, and he's been apologising for it ever since. "The damp," he says, to everyone. He's thinner than he was. You hadn't noticed until now.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] == 2}[who:young-man] is huddled by the haulers' fire with his knees drawn up, sweat on his face and his teeth chattering. The cough comes from somewhere low now, and takes a long time to stop. "It's the damp," he says. "Everyone's got it."{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-sickness] >= 3}[who:young-man] doesn't get up from the fire today. He lies on his side under a blanket, breathing short, and the cough shakes the whole length of him. [who:regard-rope-mother] has put a cup of water by his head. There's nothing else anyone here can give him.{/if}{if [q:prologue-young-man-cared] >= 2} He looks up when he sees it's you.{/if}

branches.title: Give him something to eat
branches.description: Give him something to eat from your provisions, and watch him eat it.

success.title: Something in him
success.description: He says he isn't hungry, and eats all of it. Slowly, a mouthful at a time, with a rest between. "Don't tell the old woman," he says. "She'll think I'm going soft."

branches.title: Swap places with him by the fire
branches.description: Swap places with him, so he has the side of the fire out of the wind.

success.title: The warm side
success.description: He argues, and loses. The warm side, and his back to the wind-break, and in a while he stops shivering. The wind finds you instead.

branches.title: Walk him to the surgeon by the road
branches.description: There's a surgeon under an awning by the road. Get his arm over your shoulder, and walk him there.

success.title: No seal
success.description:
The surgeon looks at the young man's neck before he looks at his face. No seal. "Not a fever," he says. "Not on my table. If he dies there, nobody comes for him, and he gets up on it." He dries his hands. "[who:surgeon]. Keep him warm, and get bread into him. That's all anybody can do, out here."

Walking back, [who:young-man] is quiet for once. Then: "Could've told you."

branches.title: Sit with him a while
branches.description: Sit with him a while, and let the camp go by.

success.title: Company
success.description: You don't talk much. He points out people as they pass: the drover who sings to his dead, the girl who sells the same eel twice. Once he falls asleep against your shoulder, and wakes up embarrassed, and coughs to cover it.

through-the-gate.title: Into the City
through-the-gate.intro:
{if [q:prologue-smuggled-in] > 0}The alley behind the dyer's runs blue and red into the gutter. You wring out what you can of your clothes. Your hands are shaking, and you're in, and nobody in here holds your death.{else}{if [q:prologue-wardens-felt-the-cold] > 0}It's the same warden. He holds your hands longer than he needs to, and looks at your face, and says nothing at all. Then he turns your hand to the light to read your mark, and steps aside.{else}{if [q:claim] == 2}The warden holds your hands a moment and barely glances at your brow: barge, handbell, hand, burned where the nail will go. "Company," he says, and you're waved into the arch with the drovers and the dead.{/if}{if [q:claim] == 1}The warden feels your hands, then turns the right one to the light: a chapel and a nail, pricked in ink. He asks your name, and checks it against the seal at your neck. "Go on, then."{/if}{if [q:claim] == 3}{if [q:prologue-lead-the-seals] > 0}The thin warden with the broken nose{else}A thin warden with a broken nose{/if} takes your hands without looking up, lets them go, and waves you through. He never looks at the knot on your wrist.{/if}{/if}

Ten paces of dark under the wall. Cold stone, and the echo of every cart. Then the far end, and noise, and the city.{/if}

branches.title: Go on into the city
branches.description: {if [q:prologue-smuggled-in] > 0}Go up the alley, and out into the city.{else}Step out of the arch, into the city.{/if}

success.title: The city
success.description: You step out.

turned-back.title: Turned Back
turned-back.intro: The wardens are walking people back down the road from the gate, a hand on each collar. They read every mark twice now.{if [q:origin] == 3} You've seen roads like this behind an army.{/if} There's a new price for a church claim chalked on the chapel door. And a family, turned back, has put its blanket down where you sleep at the haulers' fire.

branches.title: Make room for them by the fire
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 3}The youngest is asleep on her feet. Shift your things along, and make room for them.{else}Shift your things along the log, and make room for them by the fire.{/if}

success.title: Further from the fire
success.description:
They take the warm side without being asked twice. You sleep further from the fire tonight, with somebody's elbow in your back.

[who:regard-rope-mother] watches you do it. "That's how it's done out here," she says. "Until there's no room left."

branches.title: Tell them the place is taken
branches.description: {if [q:trait] == 4}There's room at the next fire. Tell them the place is yours.{else}Tell them, as kindly as you can, that the place is taken.{/if}

success.title: They go
success.description: The father looks at you a long moment. Then he rolls up the blanket, and they go down to the next fire, and the one after that. You have your place. [who:regard-rope-mother] watches them go, and doesn't say a word to you all evening.

failure.title: They stay
failure.description: You'll say it better next time; you're learning how to make people listen. The father doesn't move. "We were turned back too," he says. "Same as you." He stays where he is, and so do the children. You sleep at the edge of the light.

branches.title: Ask the father what the wardens said
branches.description: Sit down by them, and ask the father what the wardens told him.

success.title: Read twice
success.description:
"Read my hand twice, and my name three times," he says. "Then sent us down. Company brands go through, and the rich. A church mark, they read it twice. A new mark, they won't look at." He shrugs. "Nothing on you, they don't even read."

They stay where they are, all of them. You sleep on the cold side.

under-the-dust.title: Under the Dust
under-the-dust.intro: Near the arch, the queue stops, and the dust settles. You pull your scarf down off your face. Underneath:

branches.title: A woman
branches.description: A woman's face, burned brown by the road. A woman, all the way through.

success.title: A woman
success.description: The carter behind you calls you "mistress", and asks where your man is. You let the question go past you, like the dust.

branches.title: A man
branches.description: A man's face, a beard grown on the road. A man.

success.title: A man
success.description: A recruiter's boy walks the queue with a drum, looking at shoulders. He looks at yours for a long time.

branches.title: More than the queue can see
branches.description: The face under the dust is one thing. Who you are is another.

success.title: More than it sees
success.description: You keep the scarf in your hand.

what-people-see.title: What People See
what-people-see.intro: Below the camp the river runs slow and brown along the bank, and a woman is filling a bucket further along. You kneel to wash the road off your face. The water stills, and gives your face back to you.

branches.title: Young
branches.description: Young. Not yet twenty, whatever you tell people.

success.title: Young
success.description: A face the road has hardly marked. The woman with the bucket calls you "chick", and means it kindly. People will, for a few years yet.

branches.title: Grown
branches.description: Grown. Somewhere between twenty and forty, in the middle of your strength.

success.title: Grown
success.description: The road has put lines round your eyes, and taken nothing else. Grown folk get no questions below the wall, and no help either. You're used to both.

branches.title: Older
branches.description: Older. Past forty, and your knees know it.

success.title: Older
success.description: More grey than you remember. Your knees complain on the wet stones, and getting up again takes longer than it did.

branches.title: Old
branches.description: Old. Past sixty, which few people below this wall will ever be.

success.title: Old
success.description: All bone and weather. The woman with the bucket stops to look at you. "Before," she says. "You remember before." It isn't a question.

what-the-river-gives.title: What the River Gives
what-the-river-gives.intro: A hauler's girl comes up the river steps with her skirt held up in front of her, full of something that moves: crayfish, out of the shallows below the rapids. She sees you looking. "There's eels in the old rope-gang traps, if you know which ones are ours. Cress, past the mills. Mussels, if you go far enough down." She weighs you up. "I'm going back down. You can carry the bucket."

branches.title: Go down with her
branches.description: Go down with her, and carry the bucket.{if [q:origin] == 2} You know eel traps. You set them yourself, once, off the towpath.{/if}

success.title: A handful of crayfish
success.description: She takes you along the bank to where the old traps are tied, and which ones are the haulers', and which ones somebody will knife you for. Under the stones below the rapids, you turn up crayfish faster than she does. She lets you keep a handful. "You'll do," she says. "Same time tomorrow, if you want. Go on your own after that."

failure.title: In up to the waist
failure.description: Your eyes learn the river as you go: where the water is slow, where the stones hide things. Then the bank gives way under you, and you're in up to the waist, and she laughs so hard she has to sit down. She shows you the traps anyway, while you drip. "Go on your own, next time," she says. "Quieter."

branches.title: Ask her where to look
branches.description: Ask her where to look, and pay her for it. Your boots stay dry.

success.title: A coin's worth of secrets
success.description: She bites the coin, then tells you: which traps are the haulers', which ones somebody will knife you for, where the cress grows, how far down the mussels are. "Don't tell anyone it was me," she says, and goes back down the steps with her skirt full.

what-you-came-for.title: What You Came For
what-you-came-for.intro:
You stop where the street gives out over the river, with the rapids roaring white below. Bread is dear in here too: the queues say so, and the shut faces in them. Nobody looks at you twice.{if [q:keepsake-company-seal] > 0} Your mother's seal sits inside your shirt.{/if}{if [q:prologue-bound-the-young-man] > 0 && [q:prologue-released-the-young-man] == 0}{if [q:prologue-hired-out-the-young-man] > 0} Outside the wall, [who:young-man] is turning a mill wheel in the company's yard, for your coin.{else} Outside the wall, [who:young-man] is still standing where you left him.{/if}{/if}

The reason you walked all this way comes back to you, plain as hunger.

branches.title: Put them to rest
branches.description: To find someone you lost, who works bound somewhere in this city, and buy their release.
branches.hoverText: Your aspiration: find someone you lost, who works bound somewhere, and buy their release.

success.title: A face you know
success.description: Somewhere in these streets, in a row, in a yard, there's a face you know, with a seal nailed to its brow, still walking to a bell. You'll find it. Then you'll find the money.

branches.title: Rise
branches.description: To rise. To be the one who stamps the seals, not the one who wears them.
branches.hoverText: Your aspiration: stamp the seals, not wear them. In the church, a company, or the council.

success.title: Something to hold
success.description: The company man with his ledger. The binder with her stamp. The wardens who took the rider in through the gate. Everyone who matters here holds something. You'll hold something too. You haven't decided what yet.

branches.title: Get even
branches.description: To get even. Someone took your place: your work, your home, your dead. Make them pay.
branches.hoverText: Your aspiration: someone took your place. Make them pay.

success.title: Where you'll start
success.description: They're in this city. You don't know where yet, or how, or what paying will look like. But you know their name, or their mark, and that's where you'll start.

where-you-come-from.title: Where You Come From
where-you-come-from.intro: In the lee of a hand-cart, out of the wind, you untie your bundle and lay it all out. A coat, rolled tight. A purse. The end of a loaf. And at the bottom, folded small, your own clothes.

branches.title: The farmlands
branches.description: Shake out the homespun, mended at the knees. It still smells of the hayloft, and of the fields downriver that the dead plough now.
branches.hoverText: Brawn and Fieldcraft. Townspeople take you for simple.

success.title: The farmlands
success.description:
You watched them plough the long field from the hedge: eight bound in a line, a drover with a handbell, furrows straighter than your father ever cut. Nobody needed you after that. You pull the homespun on over your head, and roll the road shirt into the bundle.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

branches.title: The river
branches.description: Unroll the canvas and leather, worn through at the shoulder where the tow-rope sat.
branches.hoverText: Brawn and Nerve. Respectable people look down on haulers.

success.title: The river
success.description:
The company paid the gang off on a Tuesday, a coin each and a handshake. On the Wednesday their dead were on the rope, and the barge went faster. You shrug the canvas on, and roll the road shirt into the bundle. Your shoulder still has the groove.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

branches.title: The wars
branches.description: Shake out the soldier's jacket from the edge wars: slashed sleeves, faded colours, and a stain on the cuff that never came out.
branches.hoverText: Arms and Shot. People fear soldiers, and need them.

success.title: The wars
success.description:
Three summers in the edge wars. A pike in a line of living men, a line of bound dead in front to take the first charge, and another line of dead coming at it. Then your company was paid off, or you left. It comes to the same. The jacket still fits.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

branches.title: A broken town
branches.description: Pull out what you walked out of the dead lands in: torn, stained, and not all of it yours.
branches.hoverText: Fieldcraft and Nerve. People pity you, and keep their distance.

success.title: A broken town
success.description:
The town's binder died in the night, of age. By morning every bound in the town was loose: the mill hands, the carters, your neighbour's grandfather. You walked out through the fields with the church bell still going behind you. Something was pulling the bell rope. You put the rags back on. They're what you have.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

branches.title: Another city
branches.description: Unfold the clerk's black: good cloth, brushed thin, wrapped round an empty pen case. A small city's clothes, for a bigger one.
branches.hoverText: Letters and Guile. Labourers don't trust you.

success.title: Another city
success.description:
You can read, write and keep your mouth shut, which is three more things than most people on this road. In a small city that gets you a stool. In this one, you've heard, it gets you further. You sold the stool. You put the black on, and look like somebody again.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

branches.title: The church
branches.description: Unfold the novice's grey, with the badge picked off. The threads still show where it was.
branches.hoverText: Rites and Letters. The church remembers who leaves.

success.title: The church
success.description:
You know the prayer for the bound by heart, and the prayer at an unbinding, and what the chapel charges for each. You left before the vows. The church lets people leave. It writes down who. You put the grey on, and keep your back to the chapel.

[The Kit tab shows what you wear. A coat goes on and off anywhere, whenever no card is open. A whole change of clothes needs a place to change: the haulers' fire has one.]

who-you-are.title: Who You Are
who-you-are.intro:
In the camp's road, the company's crier has a big pot on a cart: free stew, for anyone who'll stand still and hear him out. Two of the company's bound ladle it. Half the camp is in the queue, [who:regard-rope-mother] too. "Free is free," she says.

[What you do here sets your character's trait. It opens some choices and closes others for the rest of the game, and people notice it.]

branches.title: Devout
branches.description: As the bound ladle out the stew, bow your head over them, and say the prayer for the bound aloud, the way the chapel taught it.
branches.hoverText: Devout: church choices open to you, and priests trust you. Heresy disturbs you.

success.title: The prayer for the bound
success.description: "...and shorten their labour." A few in the queue mutter along with you. The crier waits, smiling, until you're done. "Our chaplain says those very words over every one of ours," he says. The bound don't look up.

branches.title: Doubter
branches.description: The crier swears the company's chaplain prays over every soul on its books. Laugh out loud.
branches.hoverText: Doubter: you see through the church, and heretics seek you out. You can't fake devotion.

success.title: No prayer
success.description: Somebody further down the queue laughs with you. The crier doesn't. [who:regard-rope-mother] looks at you over her bowl. "True," she says. "Say it inside the walls, and they'll find you a shift of your own."

branches.title: Soft-hearted
branches.description: A girl at the back of the queue has no bowl to hold out. Give her yours, and go to the back of the queue yourself.
branches.hoverText: Soft-hearted: more choices with the suffering, and people trust you sooner. Walking past costs you.

success.title: Your bowl
success.description: She eats it standing, fast, watching you as if you might change your mind. By the time you reach the pot again, it's scraped bare. [who:regard-rope-mother] hands you her own bowl, half full. "You'll do," she says.

branches.title: Hard-hearted
branches.description: The man in front of you coughs, wet and deep, over the pot. Step round him, and take his place.
branches.hoverText: Hard-hearted: pleas don't move you, and cruel bargains are open to you. Trust comes slowly.

success.title: His place
success.description: He lets you. He hasn't the breath to argue. The bound fill your bowl, and somebody behind you says the sick are people too. [who:regard-rope-mother] watches you go by. "Careful," she says. "Careful lives long, out here."

branches.title: Proud
branches.description: Step out of the queue. You're not here for the company's charity.
branches.hoverText: Proud: you can demand and challenge. You can't beg.

success.title: Not charity
success.description: The crier calls after you that it's no charity: the company feeds its own. That's worse. Your stomach argues with you all the way back to the fire.

branches.title: Grasping
branches.description: Count the bound, the bowls and the queue, and ask the crier what a bound man earns the company in a day.
branches.hoverText: Grasping: you see what things are worth, and you get more chances to profit. Coin tempts you at bad moments.

success.title: What a dead man earns
success.description: "More than you ever will," he says, and laughs. "And he never needs feeding, and he never asks for more." You find yourself doing the sum. [who:regard-rope-mother] watches you do it.

branches.title: Curious
branches.description: Ask the crier why the company gives stew away, with the fleet late and bread up a penny.
branches.hoverText: Curious: you're quick to work things out.

success.title: Why it's free
success.description: "Because a man remembers who fed him," says the crier, "the day he needs a seal." He winks. [who:regard-rope-mother] snorts into her bowl. "He's not wrong," she says. "That's the worst of it."

branches.title: Loyal
branches.description: The crier has an arm round a hauler from your fire, and a pen out. Go and stand beside the hauler.
branches.hoverText: Loyal: allies stand by you. Betraying someone who trusts you costs far more.

success.title: He's thinking about it
success.description: "He's thinking about it," you say. The crier looks at you, then at [who:regard-rope-mother], and puts his pen away. The hauler grins at you, red to the ears. "You stand by people," she says. "That costs, here."

branches.title: Hot-tempered
branches.description: One of the bound turns with the ladle and slops stew down your front. Shove him back, hard.
branches.hoverText: Hot-tempered: violent choices appear, and you intimidate. Backing down is hard.

success.title: Like shoving a door
success.description: It's like shoving a door. The bound man doesn't look at you. The crier's men do: two of them walk you out of the queue, and there's no stew for you today. "They don't care," [who:regard-rope-mother] says as you pass. "Waste of a good temper."

branches.title: Teetotal
branches.description: A boy comes down the queue with a jug, to drink the company's health. Pass it on without drinking.
branches.hoverText: Teetotal: a clear head at night. Taverns, toasts and drink's escapes are closed to you.

success.title: A clear head
success.description: The boy shrugs. The man behind you drinks your swallow and his own. [who:regard-rope-mother] watches the jug go by. "Clear head," she says. "You'll want one, for the seals. Most folk drink to forget what they've signed."

branches.title: Hearty appetite
branches.description: Eat fast, and be back in the queue with your bowl before the pot's scraped.
branches.hoverText: Hearty appetite: meals give you more. Hunger comes faster.

success.title: Seconds
success.description: The bound man fills it again without a flicker. The crier laughs. "There's a mouth! We feed our people like that every night, in the yards." [who:regard-rope-mother] snorts. You eat the second bowl slower.

branches.title: Grave-shy
branches.description: When the bound man holds out the ladle to you, step back, and ask the crier to serve you himself.
branches.hoverText: Grave-shy: you notice the signs of the dead first. Facing the dead is harder.

success.title: Out of their way
success.description: The crier looks at you as if you'd asked him to kneel, and serves you. The bound man's hand stays out a moment, empty, then goes back to the pot. Your skin crawls until you're three tents away. "They don't do anything," [who:regard-rope-mother] says. "Not with a nail in them."

word-from-the-ford.title: Word from the Ford
word-from-the-ford.intro: Shouting, down the road. A rider is coming up from the ford, where the fleet was due, on a horse lathered to the knees, and the whole camp runs to meet him. A boy in a drover's coat, white to the lips, blood dried down one sleeve. Two wardens are pushing down from the gate to reach him. He's talking, fast, to anyone who'll listen. You can't hear him from here.

branches.title: Push through to hear him
branches.description: Push through the crowd, and get close enough to hear him.

success.title: They turned round
success.description:
"—an arrow, from the trees, in the binder's neck, and he went down in the water, and then all of them, all at once, every one on every rope—"

The wardens have his arms.

"—they turned round," he says, as they walk him up the road to the gate. "They turned round on us."

failure.title: One word
failure.description: You shove and shout with everyone else, and come out of it with a voice that carries further. Then an elbow, a shoulder, and you're back where you started. All you get is one word, passed back over the heads from mouth to mouth: *lost*. The fleet's lost.

branches.title: Listen to the crowd
branches.description: Stay where you are, and listen to the crowd instead.

success.title: Everyone's sure
success.description:
The fleet's lost, says everyone. Lost at the ford, says a carter. The reformers did it, says a woman with a church seal: they'd free every dead in the world and let the living starve. The company did it, says a hauler, for the price of bread.

Nobody saw anything. Everyone's sure.

your-mark.title: Your Mark
your-mark.intro: {if [q:mark-fresh] >= 3}The new mark throbs with your pulse{if [q:claim] == 2}, there on your brow, where the nail will go{/if}{if [q:claim] == 1}, on the back of your hand{/if}{if [q:claim] == 3}, inside your wrist{/if}. It isn't like a cut. There's nothing to clean and nothing to stitch: a mark heals in its own time, and until it does, no warden can read it.{/if}{if [q:mark-fresh] == 2}The mark has crusted over in the night. It itches, and you mustn't scratch it, and your hand keeps finding it anyway. Still too raw for any warden to read. There's nothing to do for it but wait.{/if}{if [q:mark-fresh] == 1}The scab is lifting at the edges, and under it the mark is dark and clean. Nearly healed. Soon the wardens will be able to read it, and you'll never be rid of it.{/if}

branches.title: Look at it properly
branches.description: Look at it properly, and think about what it means.

success.title: What it means
success.description: {if [q:claim] == 2}Barge, handbell, hand. When you die, the company's cart will come for you, and a company binder will drive the nail in through this very spot, and you'll go out of the yard gate at Prime with the rest of them until you wear out. Until then they'll work you, and everyone in the city will know what you are before they know your name. Two coin. You took them.{/if}{if [q:claim] == 1}A chapel and a nail. When you die, the chapel's cart will come for you, and you'll work a term in the church's yards for your sins, whatever they turn out to be. Then a binder like [who:regard-binder] will draw the nail and let you lie. A term. Nobody will tell you how long. You paid for it.{/if}{if [q:claim] == 3}The club's knot. When you die, someone will cry it at the fire, and the club's binder will come the same hour and let you go. Nobody works you, not for a day. In return you're theirs while you live: their quarrels, their dead to carry, and the dues every few days. Miss them once, and the knot gets a line through it.{/if}

branches.title: Cover it
branches.description: Cover it: a rag, a cuff pulled down, a hood. For now.

success.title: What it hides
success.description: {if [q:claim] == 2}You tie a rag round your head like someone with a fever. It hides the brand and nothing else: below the wall, a rag round the brow means one thing, and the woman at the next fire looks at it and then away. You'll wear it under your hair, under a hat, for the rest of your life. It will still be there when the nail goes in.{/if}{if [q:claim] == 1}You pull your cuff down over the back of your hand. Nobody in the camp would look twice at a church mark. Inside the walls, they say, the rich wear only a seal, and nothing on the skin at all. Your hand will never be that hand now.{/if}{if [q:claim] == 3}You push your sleeve down over your wrist. A hauler at the fire sees you do it and laughs, not unkindly, and pushes up his own sleeve to show you his knot, gone blue and blurred with the years. "You get used to it," he says. "Then you're proud of it."{/if}

your-stomach.title: Your Stomach
your-stomach.intro:
Your stomach is a fist. You can't remember the last thing you ate, and you can't think about anything else. There's bread tucked in your belt.

[Eating uses your Provisions. You can also eat at a place that offers it, such as the haulers' fire, once a day.]

branches.title: Not now
branches.description: Not now. Save it.

success.title: Belt tighter
success.description: You pull your belt a notch tighter, and try not to think about the bread.

branches.title: Eat something
branches.description: Eat some of what you carry, now.

success.title: Bread
success.description: Stale bread and the end of an onion, eaten standing up. It's the best thing you've ever tasted.

decks.title: The Camp
decks.description: Tents, fires and rumours below the wall, and the dead going out to work.

closed.reason: The camp is dark. Only the fires, and the dead-yards' lanterns.

decks.quiet: {if [q:origin] == 0}Your bundle is still tied on your back, as it was on the road.{else}The camp has nothing more for you today.{/if}

decks.title: Sleep
decks.description: The night. Dealt when you rest; never drawn.

below-the-wall.title: Below the Wall
below-the-wall.description: The camp below the land gate, where arrivals wait for a claim: tents, fires, the dead-yards downwind. The wind off the river finds every gap in a coat.

the-city.title: The City
the-city.description: The old city at the rapids. Walls older than anyone's records, and bells at every hour. Cold in the shade of the walls, and damp off the rapids.

the-road.title: The Road In
the-road.description: The last mile of the river road, under the city's walls. Autumn: a cold wind comes up off the water.

aspiration-advances.title: The aspiration advances
aspiration-advances.message: The character's aspiration moves a step closer.

the-young-mans-hire.title: The young man's hire
the-young-mans-hire.message: The company man's boy finds you at first light with two coin: [who:young-man]'s hire.

terms.title: The bound
terms.text: The dead, with a seal nailed to the skull. They obey, and do the heavy work: haul, dig, row, carry.

terms.title: Binding
terms.text: The rite that makes a corpse obey: the seal it wore in life is laid on the brow, and an iron nail is driven through it. It costs the one who does it.

terms.title: Drover
terms.text: Someone who works the bound dead for hire. Some drovers have a few dead, and some have many.

terms.title: Wardens
terms.text: The council's guards on the walls and the gates, in red.

terms.title: Claim
terms.text: The right to a person's body when they die, and the duty to come for it. Most people carry it as a mark on the skin and a seal at the neck, both with the holder's sign. The rich carry only the seal.

terms.title: The risen
terms.text: The dead that get up unbound. Take the head, or burn them.

terms.title: Binder
terms.text: Someone who binds the dead. Their hands are always cold.

terms.title: Unbinding
terms.text: Drawing the nail and the seal from a bound corpse, so it lies still for good. Anyone can do it, and it is a crime: the bound belong to someone.

terms.title: A breaking
terms.text: When a binder dies, every corpse they held goes loose at once, unless another binder takes them over fast.

terms.title: The dead lands
terms.text: Country where a breaking let the dead loose, and nobody went back.
